The Afdeling notes that constitutional questions on the partial or full lapse of COVID-19 measures involve citizens' constitutionally protected rights, requiring careful legislation.

35892.s: The bill strengthens criminal and administrative tools against animal cruelty, neglect and welfare breaches: it criminalises inciting animals against humans or other animals, lets the public prosecutor impose conduct directions barring animal keeping, and creates a court-imposed freestanding measure banning animal keeping for up to ten years, enforceable on pain of prosecution. It also adds ministerial educational measures, extends closure powers to animal welfare, and widens the ban on showing docked animals.
35892.j: The memorandum justifies the new powers by the high societal impact of animal cruelty cases, the need to prevent repeat offences and protect society, and the proportionality safeguards of judicial review.
q: In such a case the court may find that the suspect's right to move freely weighs less than the interest of a safe society or of animals being protected from cruelty and neglect.

De rechter kan in zo'n geval oordelen dat het recht van de verdachte om zich vrij te bewegen minder zwaar weegt dan het belang van een veilige maatschappij of het belang van dieren om gevrijwaard te zijn van mishandeling en verwaarlozing.
d: Artikel III, onderdelen A en D (artikelen 2.15, 2.16 en 8.6 Wet dieren)
designating further prohibited physical interventions on animals
Artikel III, onderdeel B (artikel 5.10a Wet dieren)
educational measures for animal keepers (courses or training)
p: Artikel III, onderdeel B (artikel 5.10a Wet dieren)
The Minister may impose educational measures, including mandatory courses, on animal keepers who have not complied with the Act, with content set case by case by the supervisor.
Artikel III, onderdeel F (artikel 8.11a Wet dieren)

A court may impose a keeping ban and area ban of up to ten years as a freestanding restriction of liberty, with immediate enforceability and criminal sanction for violation, subject to judicial proportionality review.
The public prosecutor may give conduct directions barring keeping animals or areas, challengeable before the court via the raadkamer procedure.
Artikel III, onderdeel C (artikel 5.12 Wet dieren)
The Minister may take closure or suspension measures against businesses and locations also where animal welfare, not only health, is at stake.

parties: Asks whether the government will monitor and report annually on how often the standalone liberty-restricting measures are imposed and for how long.
Is it possible to send an annual report to the House of Representatives describing the application of these measures in outline and in figures?
Is het mogelijk om een rapportage hiervan jaarlijks naar de Tweede Kamer te sturen, waarin deze toepassing op hoofdlijnen en ook cijfermatig wordt beschreven?
Supports the bill but asks how the effectiveness of the measures will be evaluated and how seized animals' welfare is guaranteed over the owner's punishment.
As far as the D66 members are concerned, every case of animal cruelty is one too many.
Wat de leden van de D66-fractie betreft is elk geval van dierenmishandeling er één te veel.
Criticises the long delay in the bill, the exclusion of commercial keepers from the standalone ban, the ten-year cap, and insufficient enforcement capacity for police and the inspectorate.
Asks why seizure without flagrante delicto was dropped, what practical enforcement problems follow, and how the OM will handle seized animals.
What practical implementation problems are to be expected if seizure outside flagrante delicto is not possible or pre-trial detention cannot be applied?
Welke (praktische) uitvoeringsproblemen zijn te verwachten, indien inbeslagname buiten heterdaad niet mogelijk zal zijn of voorlopige hechtenis niet toegepast kan worden?
Asks why a lifetime ban was not chosen over a maximum of ten years and how the government reflects on the bill's long delay.
Can the government extensively motivate why this option was not chosen, and only a ban of at most ten years?
Kan de regering uitgebreid motiveren waarom niet voor deze optie is gekozen, maar slechts voor een houdverbod van maximaal tien jaar?
Asks why municipalities should handle bite incidents and how animal welfare is ensured while animals are held under the bill's measures.
Why does the government think it is better for municipalities to handle bite incidents?
Waarom denkt de regering dat het beter is dat gemeenten bijtincidenten afhandelen?
Welcomes the bill but questions why a longer or permanent ban was rejected as disproportionate while other countries impose permanent bans.
Why would a permanent ban be disproportionate in the Netherlands when comparable countries do not consider it so?
Waarom zou een permanent houdverbod in Nederland disproportioneel zijn, terwijl dit in vergelijkbare landen niet als zodanig wordt beschouwd?
Asks for a legal definition of animal welfare ('welzijn van dieren') to avoid disputes over its meaning.
A defined legal framework is necessary to give meaning to the concept of 'animal welfare'.
Een afgebakend juridisch kader is noodzakelijk om duiding te geven aan het begrip «welzijn van dieren».

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on the draft Wet aanpak dierenmishandeling en dierverwaarlozing, criticizing the immediate enforceability of conditions and the extended probation for a dog/animal keeping ban as a conditional sentence, and questioning the 10-year maximum duration of the standalone ban and area ban. The government's reply accepted most points: immediate enforceability for special conditions was dropped, the 10-year probation was removed, and the 10-year maximum for the standalone ban was retained with a stronger proportionality justification added to the explanatory memorandum.
concerns: The Afdeling questioned whether the 10-year maximum duration of the standalone keeping ban and area ban is proportionate and urged reducing it to five years or justifying it convincingly; the government kept ten years but added proportionality reasoning to the memorandum.

The Afdeling argued that immediate enforceability (dadelijke uitvoerbaarheid) of conditions before a final judgment is an exception to the presumption of innocence that was not justified; the government dropped immediate enforceability for special conditions.

The Afdeling found the necessity of a 10-year probation period for special conditions not convincingly justified and advised deleting it; the government removed the extended probation for animal welfare cases.

35925-V.s: This is the 2022 budget bill (Voorstel van wet) that formally establishes the departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, setting expenditure, commitments and receipts in thousands of euros. The explanatory memorandum excerpt covers foreign policy priorities, EU and Council of Europe cooperation, and consular matters, and contains no delegation of rule-making or new executive powers.
q: The departmental budget statement belonging to this law for the year 2022 is established.
De bij deze wet behorende departementale begrotingsstaat voor het jaar 2022 wordt vastgesteld.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the 2022 budget bill for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (begrotingsstaat V) and found no remarks, advising submission to the Tweede Kamer. The government's nader rapport of 20 September 2021 states that some budgets need amendments, referring to annexes, without raising any Council of State objections.

35937.s: The bill amends the 2021 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate, changing spending authorizations for COVID-19 support schemes and a renewed value-appreciation scheme. It sets the amounts in thousands of euros and provides for entry into force from 11 October 2021.
35937.j: The memorandum justifies the budget changes by lower-than-expected uptake of the COVID-19 support schemes and an improved economic situation, and requests parliamentary authorization for commitments and expenditure.
q: In this incidental supplementary budget, parliament is asked for authorization to enter into commitments and make expenditures for the schemes below.
In deze incidentele suppletoire begroting wordt het parlement om autorisatie verzocht voor het aangaan van verplichtingen en doen van uitgaven voor onderstaande regelingen.

35946.s: This omnibus bill makes many mainly technical and editorial amendments to education and culture laws, including the WEB, WVO 2020, WPO and related acts. It also changes admission, examination, school funding timing and student finance rules, without creating major new executive discretion.
35946.j: The memorandum justifies the changes mainly as technical clarifications and corrections of earlier errors, with delegations to fill in procedural detail by general administrative order or ministerial regulation.
d: ARTIKEL XIV (Wet op de expertisecentra, artikel 114, zesde lid)
annual funding amounts, calculation and payment terms for special education
ARTIKEL XVIII (Wet op het primair onderwijs, artikel 116, zesde lid)
annual funding amounts, calculation and payment schedule for primary schools
ARTIKEL XXIV (Wet voortgezet onderwijs 2020, artikel 8.24, tweede lid)
calculation and payment of regional early school-leaving allowance
ARTIKEL XXIV (Wet voortgezet onderwijs 2020, artikel 2.51a, zevende lid)
further rules on tasks of the examination secretary
ARTIKEL XXIV (Wet voortgezet onderwijs 2020, artikel 2.55a, tweede lid)
rules on providing school examination assessments to candidates
p: ARTIKEL VI (Invoerings- en aanpassingswet WVO 2020) / ARTIKEL XXIV (WVO 2020, art. 2.60b–2.60c)
School boards may depart from examination committee proposals only after consultation and written justification, and modifications to the examination programme are limited to specified grounds.
ARTIKEL XIX (Wet voortgezet onderwijs, artikel 69 en 75 WPO)
The Minister may decide to withdraw funding entitlement for a new school that fails to open within a set period, clarifying an existing procedure.

parties: Asks how compensation via the Gemeentefonds for abolishing the youth library fee was agreed and why the Chamber was not informed earlier.
Why did the Minister not inform the Chamber in the above policy response that compensation via the Gemeentefonds would be provided?
Waarom heeft de Minister in bovengenoemde beleidsreactie de Kamer niet gemeld dat hier compensatie via het Gemeentefonds voor zou komen?
Asks the government to clarify what kinds of changes to lower regulation it intends following comments from the accreditation body Verus.
Can the government explain what kind of changes it is referring to?
Kan de regering toelichten op wat voor soort wijzigingen zij doelt?
Asks whether objections raised by Stichting Leido are absent from the bill and requests a response to remaining points.
the CDA members ask whether the Minister can respond to the remaining points raised in the email from Stichting Leido
vragen de leden van de CDA-fractie of de Minister een reactie kan geven op de overige punten die naar voren worden gebracht
Asks how the government views the demands of a campaign group and whether the bill could legally regulate them.
To what extent is it possible to legally regulate these demands through the present bill?
In hoeverre is het mogelijk om middels voorliggend wetsvoorstel deze eisen wettelijk te regelen?
Welcomes free library access for all youth and asks about publicising the change to young people and parents.
Asks for a comparison of current and proposed article 7.25 WHW and the promised amendment note, given unclear scope and risk of inequality.
These members would like to receive a comparative overview of the current and proposed text of this article
Deze leden zouden graag een vergelijkend overzicht ontvangen van de huidige en de beoogde tekst van dit artikel

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the draft omnibus education, culture and media law (Verzamelwet OCW 20##) raises no substantive objections, offering only redactional remarks. The minister's reply states that four redactional remarks were adopted and one could not be implemented, and explains the added technical amendments.
concerns: Several redactional corrections in the Wet publieke gezondheid, Wet kinderopvang, Mediawet and WHW references were adopted as proposed.
The second redactional remark could not be implemented, according to the government's reply.

35964.s: The bill amends the 2021 departmental budget of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (Twelfth Incidental Supplementary Budget), adjusting expenditure and commitments, including an extension of the subsidy for unplaced cultural activities. It takes effect from 15 November 2021 with retroactive effect where the Staatsblad is published later.
q: The budget statement of the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (VIII) for the year 2021 is amended, as shown in the statement attached to this law.
De begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap (VIII) voor het jaar 2021 wordt gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat.

35973.s: The bill allows a ministerial regulation to require a COVID-19 access certificate based only on vaccination or recovery (2G) for participation in culture, events, hospitality and non-essential services, where a 3G test-based certificate is insufficient. It also creates an exemption for people who cannot medically be vaccinated, to be detailed by ministerial regulation.
35973.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation by the need to slow virus spread, protect healthcare capacity and reopen sectors safely, with the regulation subject to OMT advice and parliamentary nahang.
q: Deploying the 2G measure by ministerial regulation is only permitted if there is such a risk of transmission of the coronavirus that 3G is not sufficient.
Het inzetten van de 2G-maatregel bij ministeriële regeling mag enkel indien sprake is van een zodanig risico op transmissie van het coronavirus dat 3G niet volstaat.
d: rules on certificate use and who establishes medical exemption
alternative manner of gathering in place of 2G certificate
rules for medically exempt persons and proof of vaccination exemption
p: Allows the executive by ministerial regulation to restrict access to named sectors to vaccinated or recovered persons only, subject to necessity and nahang procedure.

parties: Asks how the House of Representatives will be involved in the AMvB and ministerial regulation and whether a shorter pre-consultation procedure is considered, stressing proportionality.
How is the House of Representatives involved in the AMvB and the MR and how can it still influence them, since much will still be elaborated in them?
Hoe wordt de Tweede Kamer betrokken bij de AMvB en de MR en hoe kan zij daar nog invloed op uitoefenen, omdat veel daarin nog uitgewerkt gaat worden?
Opposes 2G as ineffective at preventing transmission and untimely, and argues the measure pressures people and rests on misleading information.
The OMT states in its 130th advice that a coronavirus access pass is 'not a measure to prevent virus spread'.
Het Outbreak Management Team (OMT) stelt in het 130ste OMT-advies dat een coronatoegangsbewijs (ctb): «géén maatregel is om virusverspreiding te voorkomen».
Warns that restricting access for unvaccinated people is a serious infringement of fundamental rights requiring solid justification, and asks for concrete indicators for triggering 2G.
Asks whether 2G should be regulated by the heavier AMvB procedure rather than ministerial regulation, and questions how safeguards against unequal access and social effects are met.
Demands clear epidemiological thresholds and definitions of high-risk settings, and questions the government's justification and earlier statements.
When, according to the government, is the situation serious enough to justify deploying 2G?
Wanneer is er volgens de regering sprake van een dusdanige ernstige situatie dat de inzet van 2G gerechtvaardigd kan worden?
Objects to the rushed procedure and asks for a timeline, arguing the measure is disproportionate, divisive and not effective toward its stated aims.
they express disapproval of a procedure in which speed is preferred over a careful and considered treatment
spreken hun afkeuring uit over een procedure waarin vliegende vaart de voorkeur geniet boven een zorgvuldige en afgewogen behandeling
Asks for justification of the chosen regulatory route, sector-by-sector evidence, and how proportionality and subsidiarity are assessed over time.
Can the government explain how proportionality and subsidiarity are explicitly weighed while 2G is applied?
Kan de regering daarbij ingaan op welke wijze gedurende het doorlopen van het toepassen van 2G nadrukkelijk de proportionaliteit van de maatregel en het principe van subsidiariteit wordt gewogen
Considers the measure unlawful and a disproportionate infringement of fundamental rights based on vaccination status.
therefore consider the restrictions of fundamental rights and deprivations of liberty resulting from this bill wholly unlawful.
achten de grondrechtenbeperkingen en vrijheidsontnemingen, die het gevolg zijn van dit wetsvoorstel, daarom volstrekt onrechtmatig.
Views 2G as a disproportionate infringement of fundamental rights of unvaccinated people that deepens social division.
The 2G coronavirus access pass is, according to these members, a disproportionate infringement of the fundamental rights of unvaccinated people.
Het 2G coronatoegangsbewijs is volgens deze leden een disproportionele aantasting van de grondrechten van niet-gevaccineerden.
Asks the government to withdraw the bill, arguing it is less effective and unsafe compared with alternatives and may breach Article 22 of the Constitution.
therefore urgently requests the government to refrain from this bill.
verzoekt de regering daarom met klem af te zien van dit wetsvoorstel.
Asks how excluding people who can demonstrate non-infectiousness by test is compatible with the Constitution and the ECHR.
Member Omtzigt asks whether the government can explain how that would be possible under the Constitution or the European Convention on Human Rights.
Het lid Omtzigt vraagt of de regering kan aangeven hoe dat onder de Grondwet of het Europees Verdrag voor de Rechten van de Mens (EVRM) mogelijk zou zijn.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Tijdelijke wet differentiatie coronatoegangsbewijzen, which would allow 2G (vaccination or recovery only) COVID access certificates, finding the proposal not yet adequate on legal certainty, enforcement and the exception for people who cannot vaccinate. The minister's reply largely adopts the advice, tightening the statutory conditions, narrowing the scope to specified sectors, adding enforcement and exception provisions, and submits the revised bill.
concerns: The bill does not sufficiently specify in the statute which COVID certificate regime applies under which conditions, undermining legal certainty; the government added statutory conditions for 2G use.

The statute should itself define when a high-risk environment exists and when 2G is necessary and proportionate, rather than leaving this to the toelichting; the government wrote the conditions into the bill.

The relation between 2G and 3G with additional measures, and whether ondernemers may choose 3G, is unclear; the government clarified this in the statute and leaves further detail to ministerial regulation.
The option of universal testing (1G) is insufficiently examined; the government clarified that existing law already allows it and that no policy on 1G is envisaged.

Enforcement of COVID certificates is difficult and compliance is poor, so the explanatory memorandum should address concrete enforcement measures; the government added a new section on enforcement while stressing intensified efforts.

The exception for people who cannot be vaccinated needs a clear procedure and should be elaborated in the explanatory memorandum; the government supplemented the memorandum but notes implementation complexity.

35991.s: The bill adds a new article 240c to the Dutch Criminal Code that makes it a standalone offence to intentionally provide means, opportunity or information for, or to acquire or teach skills for, child sexual abuse offences against persons under sixteen, punishable by up to four years' imprisonment or a fifth-category fine. It enters into force on a date set by royal decree.
35991.j: The memorandum justifies the new offence by the need to reach online preparatory conduct and notes that police and prosecutors are equipped to investigate on the dark web.
d: date of entry into force by royal decree

parties: Supports the bill and asks about further preventive measures, enforcement gaps and the pending bestuursrechtelijke aanpak for hosting providers.
These members support this bill because a broad range of preparatory acts aimed at committing sexual abuse of a child will be made independently punishable.
Deze leden steunen dit wetsvoorstel, omdat een breed scala aan voorbereidingshandelingen met het oog op het plegen van seksueel misbruik van een kind, zelfstandig strafbaar worden gesteld.
Fully supports the aim but asks how the offence relates to existing preparatory-act rules, penalty levels and international reach.
They nevertheless still have some questions about the implementation.
Zij hebben evenwel nog enkele vragen over de uitvoering.
Asks whether punishing mere possession risks criminalising thoughts and how the offence avoids arresting people for fantasies alone.
Can the government clarify how this bill prevents people from being arrested, detained, charged and possibly convicted merely for things that exist only in their thoughts and fantasy?

Kan de regering verduidelijken op welke manier dit wetsvoorstel voorkomt dat mensen worden aangehouden, vastgehouden, beschuldigd en wellicht veroordeeld, louter vanwege zaken die zich alleen in hun gedachten en fantasie afspelen?
Supports the bill but asks whether the wording is sufficiently delimited, given concerns that the Supreme Court may require precise identification of the intended offence.
Asks why possession is not explicitly covered, about exemptions for helpers and researchers, and about anonymous reporting channels for citizens.
They ask for clarification whether merely possessing such documentation indeed falls under the scope of this law.
Zij vragen explicitering of inderdaad het louter beschikken over dergelijke documentatie onder de werking van deze wet valt.
Worries the intent requirement narrows the offence and may cause evidentiary problems, and asks about enforcement capacity and the age threshold of sixteen.
These members fear that this narrowing of the offence will lead to fewer convictions than if the offence did not require intent.
De leden van de SGP-fractie vrezen dat deze vernauwing van de strafbaarstelling leidt tot minder veroordeling dan wanneer de strafbaarstelling het opzet niet is vereist.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State welcomes the bill criminalising preparatory acts for child sexual abuse (instruction material) but questions why it is framed as a preparatory-act offence rather than a standalone offence, citing unclear intent requirements and a lex specialis departure from article 46 Sr, and advises clarifying the explanatory memorandum. The government's reply (nader rapport) largely rejects the standalone alternative, explains the choice by analogy with article 134a/240c Sr, and states that the explanatory memorandum has been supplemented and clarified accordingly.
concerns: The explanatory memorandum is ambiguous about whether intent must relate to actually committing a sexual offence, and the Afdeling asks for this to be clarified and made consistent with the bill text.
Unclear intent requirement could leave mere possession of instruction material outside the scope of the proposed offence, undermining its added value.

The Afdeling asks why a standalone offence (similar to article 240b Sr) was not chosen instead of a preparatory-act construction, and the government declines, arguing article 240c Sr analogy better fits the conduct.

The proposal is a lex specialis departing from the general preparatory-act framework of article 46 Sr, requiring special justification; the government justifies it but rejects a binding specialis relationship.

36189.s: The bill inserts a new chapter into the Wegenverkeerswet 1994 with a delegation clause allowing rules on road safety management of road infrastructure to be set by general administrative order (amvb), to implement Directive 2008/96/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1936. It also withdraws the Wet beheer rijkswaterstaatswerken and the Uitvoeringsregeling verkeersveiligheid van weginfrastructuur.
36189.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation as the legal basis needed to implement the EU directive, noting the directive itself leaves little policy discretion.
q: This delegation provision makes it possible to implement the (amended) directive by or pursuant to a general administrative order (amvb).
Deze delegatiebepaling maakt het mogelijk om de (gewijzigde) richtlijn te implementeren bij of krachtens een algemene maatregel van bestuur (amvb).
d: nadere regels on road safety of road infrastructure

parties: Asks who checks compliance with road safety requirements, what consequences follow if they are not met, and why implementation requires three steps.
The VVD members read that the directive requires road safety requirements to be taken into account in the design, construction and use phases.
De leden van de VVD-fractie lezen dat de richtlijn voorschrijft dat zowel in de ontwerp-, aanleg- als gebruiksfase verkeersveiligheidseisen worden meegenomen.
Asks the government to explain the purpose, operation and content of the ministerial regulation that must enter into force as quickly as possible.
These members ask the government to further explain and justify the purpose, operation and content of the ministerial regulation.
Deze leden vragen de regering het doel, de werking en de invulling van de ministeriële regeling nader toe te lichten en te onderbouwen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill delegating power to set road traffic safety rules (implementing Directive 2008/96/EC as amended by 2019/1936) and raised concerns about the unclear scope of the delegation and the missed implementation deadline. The minister's reply accepted the scope concern by adding limits on designated roads and motivating the broader scope, and explained why the missed deadline poses no practical problems.
concerns: The delegation to designate roads by amvb lacked criteria and was too open-ended; the bill was amended to limit the designation power to at least the roads covered by the directive and specify road types in the explanatory memorandum.
The explanatory memorandum did not justify the broader scope of the delegation compared with the directive; a justification was added.
The explanatory memorandum did not substantiate that the missed implementation deadline causes no practical problems; it was updated with further explanation on the directive's effects in practice.

36198.s: The bill amends the 2022 departmental budget (begrotingsstaat) of the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport, reallocating expenditure and commitments across policy articles via an eighth supplementary budget. The explanatory memorandum concerns a COVID-19 guarantee for board liability insurance (SON) and its review framework.
q: We ... have approved and resolved ... The budget statement of the Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport for 2022 is amended
Wij Willem-Alexander ... hebben goedgevonden en verstaan ... De begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport voor het jaar 2022 wordt gewijzigd

36279.s: The bill amends article 6(1) of the Wet experiment gesloten coffeeshopketen to raise the maximum number of participating municipalities in the cannabis cultivation and coffeeshop experiment from ten to eleven. The concrete designation of the eleventh municipality is left to a future general administrative order amending the Besluit experiment gesloten coffeeshopketen.
36279.j: The memorandum justifies the eleventh municipality by the coalition agreement's commitment to add a large city to the experiment and states that the designation will be made by general administrative order.
q: In the Besluit experiment gesloten coffeeshopketen the eleventh participating municipality will be designated.
In het Besluit experiment gesloten coffeeshopketen zal de betreffende elfde deelnemende gemeente worden aangewezen.
d: designation of the eleventh participating municipality

parties: Asks about fragmented supervision among the Inspectie JenV, NVWA and mayors and the legal basis for data processing and exchange by supervisors and the research consortium.
Have further agreements also been made about this, to prevent fragmentation of supervision from occurring?
Zijn hier ook nadere afspraken over gemaakt, om te voorkomen dat er versnippering van het toezicht plaatsvindt?
Expresses concern about the delay of the experiment and asks how the backlog will be made up, while favouring full legalisation of the coffeeshop chain.
At the same time, these members have serious concerns about the accumulated delay in the experiment.
Tegelijkertijd maken deze leden zich ernstige zorgen over de opgelopen vertraging van het experiment.
Asks why the first legal cannabis experiment is still delayed, whether further delays are expected, and whether pilot municipalities may proceed.
Is it correct that the current planning is now no earlier than 2024?
Klopt het dat de huidige planning nu niet eerder dan 2024 is?
Objects to Breda and Tilburg starting on their own, which would create unequal situations and different enforcement regimes, and asks about the consequences of deviating from common conditions.
They find this highly undesirable, as it would create unequal situations.
Zij vinden dit zeer onwenselijk gezien hiermee ongelijke situaties worden gecreëerd.
Opposes the experiment, questions starting before evaluation criteria are set, the unclear cost-benefit basis, and what 'leading' outcomes means for government policy.
These members ask the government how it is possible that an experiment has already started without the conditions for assessment having been set.
Deze leden vragen de regering hoe het mogelijk is dat een experiment reeds gestart is zonder dat de voorwaarden voor de beoordeling vastgesteld zijn.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division raised one minor remark: the explanatory memorandum to the bill adding an eleventh municipality to the closed coffeeshop experiment should justify why no internet consultation was held. The government's reply supplemented the explanatory memorandum, arguing consultation could not materially change a bill that only adds one municipality.
concerns: The explanatory memorandum should motivate why internet consultation was omitted, given the government's own consultation principles.

36288.s: The bill amends the Wmo 2015 to introduce a residence-based principle (woonplaatsbeginsel) for sheltered housing, so that the municipality where a person has their registered address, or a designated fallback municipality, is responsible for providing it. It also adds a legal basis for processing sensitive personal data for this assessment and for joint procurement of certain forms of sheltered housing by municipalities.
36288.j: The memorandum justifies the new AMvB and ministerial-regulation powers by the need for a workable residence rule and by the earlier joint-procurement and cooperation arrangements, and it states that the implementation and effects will be monitored and evaluated after two years.
q: The bill further provides that for a resident who, when announcing the need for sheltered housing, has his residential address in an institution designated by ministerial regulation, the municipality where he had his residential address immediately before that stay is responsible for providing sheltered housing.

Het wetsvoorstel regelt voorts dat voor een ingezetene die, op het moment van het kenbaar maken van de behoefte aan beschermd wonen, zijn woonadres heeft in een bij ministeriële regeling aangewezen instelling, de gemeente waaraan hij onmiddellijk voorafgaand aan dit verblijf zijn woonadres had, verantwoordelijk is voor de verstrekking van beschermd wonen.
d: designating forms of sheltered housing for joint procurement and regional areas
ARTIKEL I, C (artikel 1.2.1a, eerste lid, onderdeel b)
designating institutions whose residence does not count as a residential address
p: An AMvB may designate forms of sheltered housing to be bought jointly and regions in which municipalities must cooperate, with an earlier consultation requirement in the explanatory memorandum but none in the provision itself.
ARTIKEL I, G and H (artikelen 5.1.a1 and 5.2.a1)
Municipalities gain authority to process health and criminal-law data of clients and to share such data with another municipality for residence-based assessments, limited to what is necessary.

parties: Asks whether the government will seek renewed Raad van State advice given its critical advice on the bill, given the vulnerable group affected.
These members ask why no further advice was requested from the Council of State to assess whether the amendments resolved the objections raised.
Deze leden vragen waarom geen nader advies van de Raad van State is gevraagd om te bezien of de doorgevoerde wijzigingen ertoe leidden dat voorgenoemde bezwaren zijn komen te vervallen.
Questions the government's rationale for the bill, the lack of evidence for the claimed incentive effect and the basis for the distribution model.
Why would extra budget from sheltered housing for people with a serious psychiatric condition create that incentive when the Wmo 2015 did not?
Waarom zou extra budget, afkomstig uit beschermd wonen voor mensen met een ernstige psychische aandoening (EPA), die prikkel wel tot stand brengen?
Asks how the government will prevent municipalities from scaling down specialist facilities and how client rights and capacity are protected.
How will the government prevent specialist sheltered housing facilities from disappearing?
Hoe gaat de regering voorkomen dat specialistische voorzieningen voor beschermd wonen zullen verdwijnen?
Worries that the burden of proof on residence falls on vulnerable clients and that the bill may cause new problems for care access.
Doubts that decentralisation to municipalities is still the right scale given experience since 2015 and critical reports, and fears harm to vulnerable people.
Can the government explain why it still considers the municipality the right scale for sheltered housing given current knowledge?
Kan de regering uitleggen waarom zij vinden dat de gemeente nog steeds de juiste schaal is voor de uitvoering van beschermd wonen met de kennis van nu?
Questions whether decentralisation is still justified and whether regional cooperation would work better than municipal responsibility.
Why would that mean every municipality must arrange this itself, when it could be arranged equally well or better regionally?
Waarom zou dat betekenen dat iedere gemeente dat zelf helemaal moet regelen en dit niet net zo goed of beter in regioverband geregeld kan worden?
Asks how the client's preference is weighed in choosing the place of care and what happens if the other municipality refuses, and questions the need for the bill.
What guarantee does a client have that their preference will be followed?
Welke waarborg heeft een cliënt dat zijn of haar voorkeur wordt gevolgd?
Supports the ambition of local inclusion but questions the residence criterion, its definitions and the handling of forms of care outside the scheme.
They ask for further explanation of why a residence-place principle was chosen rather than the standard residence criterion in article 2.3.5.
Zij vragen om extra toelichting waarom gekozen is voor een woonplaatsbeginsel en niet voor aansluiting bij de standaardregeling zoals beschreven in artikel 2.3.5, het ingezetenecriterium.
Notes the bill was not revised in response to the Raad van State's critical advice and asks what concrete problem is solved and whether the system becomes simpler.
Can the government indicate on which points the explanatory memorandum and the proposal were amended following the Council of State's advice?
Kan de regering aangeven op welke punten de toelichting en het voorstel zijn aangepast naar aanleiding van het advies van de Raad van State?
Sceptical that the bill delivers inclusion; warns of administrative burden, stigma and clients being shunted between municipalities, and calls for a broader integral approach first.
The BBB member is therefore critical of the bill and considers that many preconditions must be met before the residence-place principle can be introduced.

Het lid van de BBB-fractie is dan ook kritisch op het voorliggende wetsvoorstel en vindt dat om het principe van het woonplaatsbeginsel in te kunnen voeren eerst aan veel randvoorwaarden voldaan moet zijn.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering advised on a bill introducing the woonplaatsbeginsel for beschermd wonen (sheltered housing) and decentralising its funding to all municipalities, warning of risks to specialist provision, financing and regional cooperation, and advising against proceeding until these are addressed. The government's nader rapport accepts most concerns, adding mandatory regional cooperation and joint procurement via AMvB, a national arrangement for specialist facilities, and a revised bill, while disputing some points such as the need for a domicile-dispute maatregel.
concerns: The Afdeling warned that without clarity on finances and regional cooperation, the availability of (specialist) sheltered housing is at real risk, advising a less voluntary approach to decentralisation.
The Afdeling advised that decentralisation should only proceed once regions demonstrate necessary preconditions such as finances, housing and expertise, with continuity assured.

The Afdeling advised a mandatory national arrangement for the very limited number of specialist sheltered-housing facilities; the government adopted a Landelijk Transitiearrangement organised by VNG and an AMvB option for joint procurement.

The Afdeling held that the client should not bear consequences of inter-municipal disagreement over the woonplaatsbeginsel and advised clarifying that the receiving municipality decides and the responsible one bears costs; the government rejected a domicile-dispute maatregel but pointed to a geschillencommissie and doorzendplicht.

The Afdeling asked for explanation of how practical consequences (integrated client support, registration, eigen bijdrage, housing agreements) would be resolved; the government responded with a handreiking, CAK ICT adjustments and clarifications in the memorie van toelichting.

The Afdeling advised that the Minister of Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties should co-sign the bill because it concerns municipal finances and regional cooperation; the government agreed to co-sign.
The Afdeling's redactional remark on the woonadres/briefadres terminology in the explanatory memorandum was incorporated.

36369.s: The bill implements EU Directive 2022/2523 on a global minimum tax for multinational and large domestic groups, introducing a domestic top-up tax, an income inclusion top-up tax and an undertaxed profits top-up tax in Dutch law. It sets detailed definitions, scope thresholds, tax-residence rules and computation rules, with much of the technical detail left to later regulation.
36369.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by saying the simplified calculations must first be agreed in the Inclusive Framework and then set out in an AMvB, so detail cannot be fixed in the statute yet.
q: Once agreement is reached in the IF on the simplified calculations, rules will be laid down by or pursuant to a general administrative order (AMvB) to fill in the simplified calculation.

Zodra in het IF overeenstemming is bereikt over de vereenvoudigde berekeningen, zullen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur (AMvB) regels worden opgesteld voor de invulling van de vereenvoudigde berekening.
d: recognition of third-state rules as equivalent to inclusion rule
rules for requests for binding decision on filing entity
simplified calculations for undertaxed profits top-up tax
p: Safe-harbour rules leave precise content to be worked out in later administrative guidance, widening executive discretion over tax liability.

parties: Asks for detailed overviews, examples and clarity on whether later OECD guidance would automatically apply, and questions how parliament can assess complex amendments it cannot review.

Can the government reflect on how this House can guarantee the quality of this very complex legislation if it can be substantively amended during or even after the treatment of this bill, without this House being able to assess those amendments?

Kan de regering voorts reflecteren over de vraag hoe deze Kamer de kwaliteit van deze zeer complexe wetgeving kan waarborgen als deze tijdens of zelfs na de behandeling van dit wetsvoorstel inhoudelijk kan worden gewijzigd, zonder dat deze Kamer deze wijzigingen kan beoordelen?
Welcomes the bill but asks how it is ensured that countries apply and enforce the minimum tax in the same way and that the Belastingdienst can verify taxes paid abroad.
These members ask how it is ensured that countries apply and also enforce the minimum tax for multinationals in the same way.](ok)
Deze leden vragen daarnaast hoe erop wordt toegezien dat landen op eenzelfde manier de minimumbelasting voor multinationals toepassen en ook handhaven.
Supports the goal but worries about complexity, administrative burden, ICT risks at the tax authority, and unresolved dispute resolution and safe harbour rules.
These members understand that the directive must be implemented, but also ask how the government intends to deal with possible problems for the Tax Authority and ICT in implementing the law.
Deze leden begrijpen dat de richtlijn zal moeten worden geïmplementeerd, maar vragen ook hoe de regering wil omgaan met mogelijke problemen voor de Belastingdienst en ICT bij uitvoering van de wet.
Enthusiastic about curbing multinational tax avoidance but asks how the tax authority will check whether the income inclusion rule is applied and how disputes between tax authorities are resolved.
These members ask the government how any disputes between national tax authorities, for example over sufficient top-up taxation and who has that right, will be resolved.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering hoe eventuele geschillen tussen nationale belastingdiensten, bijvoorbeeld over het voldoende bijheffen en wie dat recht heeft, worden opgelost.
Welcomes the agreement to reduce tax competition and asks about the choice of fiscal rather than accounting profit and possible avoidance through excluded entities.
It makes these members positive that after years of debate there is finally agreement to reduce tax competition and effectively tax companies.
Het stemt deze leden positief dat er na jarenlang debat eindelijke overeenstemming is om belastingconcurrentie te verminderen en bedrijven effectief aan te slaan.
Asks how the Belastingdienst checks whether top-up taxes applied by other countries are correct, and asks for impact analyses and monitoring of effective tax rates.
If a domestic top-up tax has been applied in the country of a subsidiary, how does the Belastingdienst then check whether it has been applied correctly
Als in het land van een dochteronderneming een binnenlandse bijheffing is toegepast, hoe controleert de Belastingdienst dan of deze correct is toegepast
Sees a global minimum level of taxation as a good thing and asks about regimes such as the innovation box that could push effective rates below 15 percent.
These members consider this guarantee of a global minimum level of taxation for companies a good thing.
Deze leden vinden deze waarborging van een mondiaal minimumniveau van belastingheffing voor bedrijven een goede zaak.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Wet minimumbelasting 2024 implementing EU Directive 2022/2523, raising remarks on its placement in the national tax system, the uncertain sequel for lapsed penalties and interest, the broad joint liability of group entities including foreign ones, unclear taxpayer election procedures, mutual assistance and treaty application, and the policy implications for Dutch corporate tax and treaty policy. The government's reply accepts most remarks, amends the bill and explanatory memorandum on penalties, joint liability, elections and interest, and explains its position on treaties and corporate tax policy.
concerns: Unclear treatment of partly paid assessments, penalties and interest when the power to levy a supplementary assessment lapses; government amended art. 8.4(7) and the explanatory memorandum.

Broad joint and several liability of group entities, including those abroad, is insufficiently justified and its enforceability abroad is doubtful; government explains the rationale and adds clarification but does not abandon it.
Procedure, deadlines and possibility of correction for taxpayer elections are not worked out; government added explanation in the explanatory memorandum.

Interest regime for the minimum tax deviates from the AWR without motivation and the applicable rate is not disclosed in advance; government explains the deviation and commits to aligning the rate with existing rates.
Penalty for failing the information obligation is placed in the bill rather than the AWR and its limitation period is not justified; government explains the choice and aligns the limitation period.

Uncertain applicability of existing mutual assistance instruments and bilateral treaties to the new tax and need for notification to treaty partners; government clarifies that the tax falls within treaty scope and sees no added value in notification.

Advice to clarify separately the consequences for Dutch corporate tax and treaty policy of the minimum tax; government notes the question is separate and gives a brief response on existing corporate tax reliefs.

36378.s: The bill establishes a renewed regulatory framework for electricity and gas markets, merging the Electricity Act 1998 and the Gas Act into a single Energy Act, implementing EU directives and regulations. It sets rules on supply, aggregation, peer-to-peer trade, network operator tasks, metering, data exchange, tariffs and supervision by the Autoriteit Consument en Markt.
36378.j: The memorandum justifies delegation mainly as needed for technical detail and to implement EU law, and notes that tariff regulation powers lie exclusively with the independent regulator.
d: contents and termination of supply contracts
quality of network operator task performance
supply obligation on bankruptcy of supplier
p: Licence grant, amendment and revocation is assigned directly to the independent regulator ACM rather than to the Minister by mandate.
Methods and conditions for network operators require prior approval by the regulator, with connection timelines set in them.

parties: Asks about nuclear energy treatment, technology neutrality, and capacity of the ACM to protect consumers.
These members ask whether the ACM has sufficient capacity to ensure consumers are adequately protected.
Daarnaast deze leden of er voldoende capaciteit bij de ACM is om te borgen dat consumenten voldoende worden beschermd.
Asks how the government will handle risks of peer-to-peer trade and monitoring of effects, and whether the ACM should issue model contracts.
Does the government consider it desirable that model contracts also be drawn up for such services (by the ACM)?
Vindt de regering het wenselijk dat voor dergelijke diensten ook modelcontracten worden opgesteld (door de ACM)?
Criticises shifting market risks onto consumers without adequate protection against supplier bankruptcy, and asks for a definition of vulnerable customers.
They note with great sorrow the intention to shift market risks to the consumer without adequate protection of the consumer in case of supplier bankruptcies.
Zij nemen met grote treurnis kennis van de intentie om marktrisico's bij de consument neer te leggen zonder adequate bescherming van de consument in het geval van faillissementen van leveranciers.
Asks about tariff regulation, removal of ACM power to cap unreasonable tariffs, and a possible compensation fund for consumers.
The bill lacks the power for the ACM to cap unreasonable tariffs.
In het wetsvoorstel ontbreekt de bevoegdheid voor ACM om onredelijke tarieven te maximeren.
Supports stricter supplier licensing but worries about removal of tariff safeguards, and asks whether a compensation fund is needed.
Questions the removal of the obligation to supply at reasonable tariffs and the ACM's ability to intervene where competition is insufficient.
These members place large question marks next to this.
Deze leden zetten hier grote vraagtekens bij.
Asks how broad executive powers to fill in the law by AMvB fit with democratic control, and asks about a compensation fund.
How does the government reconcile this choice with the principle of democratic control and safeguards?
Hoe verhoudt de regering deze keuze tot het principe van democratische controle en borging?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised against submitting the Energy Act bill as drafted, citing unclear separation of EU implementation from national policy, the merging of the Electricity Act and Gas Act, and gaps on consumer protection, a missing capacity test, grid investment prioritisation and energy data under the GDPR. The government's reply largely accepts the criticism, rewrites parts of the explanatory memorandum, adds a prioritisation framework and clarifies the ACM's role, while maintaining the merger and the combined implementation.
concerns: The bill mixes EU implementation, modernisation and national policy, making it unclear which provisions are binding; the government rewrote chapters 1-3 of the explanatory memorandum but kept the combined implementation.
The explanatory memorandum does not concretely explain how the bill contributes to the energy transition and CO2-poor supply goals; the government reformulated the goals in terms of the EZK budget.

Protection of vulnerable consumers lacks a definition and a regime for price intervention; the government declined a general definition but committed to further measures and a case-specific framework.
The bill lacks a capacity test (doenvermogentoets) for citizens acting actively in the electricity market; the government added a substantive assessment in the explanatory memorandum.
The term 'redelijke prijzen' in article 2.6 is unclear relative to the EU directive; the government reworded the provision to track the directive's wording on competitive prices.
Financial requirements for energy suppliers are insufficiently justified against EU law and market access; the government added a passage on consequences under EU law and market effects.
The bill gives too little guarantee of a prioritisation framework for grid investments; the government added an explicit delegation and a prioritisation framework via ministerial regulation.

Provincial and municipal regulatory powers are limited under article 6.8 and unclear in relation to regional energy infrastructure; the government clarified in the memorandum that this does not conflict.

The bill does not classify energy data as personal or non-personal, nor specify controllers, processors and legal bases under the GDPR; the government rewrote section 6.1E of the memorandum but without a full classification.

36387.s: The bill gives Dutch municipalities power to designate neighbourhoods where gas may no longer be used for building heating, by amending the Gas Act and the Omgevingswet (environment and planning act), including a mandatory heat programme, data-processing grounds and transitional provisions. It sets up framework rules to be elaborated by general administrative order (AMvB), with safeguards such as affordability and reasonable time limits.
36387.j: The memorandum justifies the new municipal powers by the failure of voluntary approaches in pilot neighbourhoods and the need for statutory levers to keep the transition affordable.
q: The pilots show that an approach based on voluntariness alone is not sufficient.
Uit de proeftuinen blijkt namelijk dat een aanpak op basis van alleen vrijwilligheid niet toereikend is.
d: Artikel II, onderdeel B (Omgevingswet art. 3.6 lid)
content and requirements of municipal heat programme
Artikel II, onderdeel C (Omgevingswet art. 4.21 lid 2 e)
general rules and municipal instruction rules on sustainable energy supply of buildings
categories of buildings or activities exempt for security of supply
Artikel I, onderdeel A (Gaswet art. 10 lid 10)
data to be recorded in the ACM public register of areas
Artikel III, onderdeel A (Energiewet art. 3.42 lid 6)
rules on notification and register data for gas-free areas
p: Municipalities may exclude gas use in an area by environmental-plan rules, displacing the gas network operator's supply obligation, subject to exemptions for security of supply.
Artikel II, onderdeel A en E (Omgevingswet art. 2.25, 20.7a)
Expands government grounds to collect and share confidential owner and connection data for the energy transition.

parties: Asks how residents' interests are protected under the designation power and how it relates to property rights, and how homeowners are protected from extra costs.
These members wonder how the interests of residents are sufficiently served by this designation power.
Deze leden vragen zich af hoe de belangen van bewoners voldoende worden gediend bij deze aanwijzingsbevoegdheid.
Supports the bill's importance and asks about coherence with the heat programme, timing of landlord incentives and whether all municipalities will meet deadlines.
These members endorse the importance of this legislative amendment.
Deze leden onderschrijven het belang van deze wetswijziging.
Argues the bill amounts to coercion of households against their will and property rights (Article 14 Constitution), questioning the proportionality of costs and the lack of guarantees.
These members note that this amounts to ordinary coercion forcing households to buy extremely expensive installations.
Deze leden constateren dat hierdoor sprake is van ordinaire dwang om zo huishoudens te verplichten om peperdure installaties aan te schaffen.
Asks how affordability and woonlastenneutraliteit are guaranteed in advance and what happens if residents cannot bear costs.
These members would rather see affordability secured at the front end so people do not get into trouble from higher-than-expected costs.
Deze leden zien liever dat aan de voorkant de betaalbaarheid is geborgd en mensen niet in de problemen komen door hoger uitvallende kosten.
Asks how the Besluit gemeentelijke instrumenten warmtetransitie will be determined and how the House is involved, and how coherence with the collective heat law is ensured.
These members ask the government to explain how the process for establishing the municipal heat transition instruments decree will look and specifically how the House will be involved.

De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering toe te lichten hoe het proces voor het vaststellen van het Besluit gemeentelijke instrumenten warmtetransitie eruit komt te zien en specifiek hoe de Kamer daarin betrokken wordt?
Asks for guarantees on affordability, a right to individual postponement of gas disconnection, legal certainty and whether the designation power will be pre-submitted to the House.

They ask whether the government can provide in the bill or subordinate rules for a solution, for example a right to individual postponement of the gas disconnection date where an owner's or resident's circumstances warrant it.

Zij vragen of de regering in het wetsvoorstel of de lagere regelgeving kan voorzien in een oplossing hiervoor, bijvoorbeeld door middel van een recht op individueel uitstel van de afsluitdatum van het aardgas indien de omstandigheden van een huiseigenaar of bewoner daartoe aanleiding geven.

Opposes the coercive character of the law and the infringement of property rights as unjust and disproportionate, and asks for alternative instruments without coercion and cost calculations for municipalities.
They also seriously worry about the property right that will be violated.
Zij maken zich ook ernstig zorgen over het eigendomsrecht dat geschonden gaat worden.

Finds legal certainty and protection of individual households insufficiently guaranteed and asks why feasibility and affordability are not anchored in the statute and why no entitlement to building-linked financing exists.
From the standpoint of fairness, legal certainty and public support, these members find the necessary safeguards for a careful process lacking in the bill.
Vanuit het oogpunt van rechtvaardigheid, rechtszekerheid en het belang van draagvlak missen deze leden in het voorliggende wetsvoorstel de noodzakelijke waarborgen voor een zorgvuldig proces.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Wet gemeentelijke instrumenten warmtetransitie, which lets municipalities designate neighbourhoods to be disconnected from gas, raising concerns on target clarity, binding nature, implementability, rights, litigation load, transitional law and coordination with the Energiewet. The government's reply largely accepts the points, adding regulation in the Bgiw and clarifications in the memorie van toelichting, while keeping the measure as a municipal power rather than a binding obligation.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for clarity on whether the bill imposes a binding obligation on municipalities to disconnect areas from gas; the government stated it is a power, not an obligation, but will regulate that a municipality which includes a neighbourhood in its warmteprogramma must in principle amend the omgevingsplan.

The Afdeling asked for clarity on the 2030 target and how the bill relates to the 1.5 million homes goal; the government clarified the target in the memorie van toelichting but did not impose a binding 2030 target.

The Afdeling asked for an analysis of shortages of materials and labour and for an assessment of municipal implementation capacity; the government pointed to existing support programmes, funding and the NPLW without a full quantitative analysis.

The Afdeling advised clarifying the position of building owners who already switched to alternative heating before the neighbourhood decision, and the government will regulate a notification duty and exemption.

The Afdeling asked for clarity on possible compensation for damage to building owners and on what counts as normal social risk versus a special burden; the government explained the criteria and referred to existing compensation framework.

The Afdeling asked for an estimate of the number of appeal procedures and consultation of the Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak; the government disagreed with the expected scale of litigation but added explanation of safeguards.

The Afdeling criticised the transitional law for transitievisies warmte as likely to force many municipalities to redo their plans; the government will replace the special transitional regime with a provision in the Bgiw aligned with the general transitional law.

The Afdeling advised adding coordination provisions with the Energiewet and clarifying the gas network operator's tasks; the government acknowledged the samenloop and committed to provisions in the Energiewet if needed.

The Afdeling advised clarifying the role of interbestuurlijk toezicht; the government explained that toezicht will apply once a binding action obligation exists in the Bgiw and the memorie van toelichting was expanded.

36486.s: The bill lets care offices (zorgkantoren) jointly fund prevention measures that reduce or postpone demand for long-term care under the Wlz, and widens the Dutch Care Authority's (NZa) power to let Wlz spending stand as lawful spending. It also introduces multi-year regional and national Wlz budget frameworks and changes appeal procedures against NZa tariff and budget decisions.
36486.j: The memorandum justifies the NZa power to let spending stand by the need for effective supervision and the care duty toward insured persons, and the amvb delegation by the need for detailed conditions on prevention measures.
q: The proposed power of the NZa is in principle limited to certain cases.
De voorgestelde bevoegdheid van de NZa wordt in beginsel beperkt tot bepaalde gevallen.
d: detailed rules for care office participation in prevention measures
rules for Zorginstituut payments from the long-term care fund and reserves
fixing the available national Wlz budget per calendar year
allocating PGB and overhead budgets across care office regions
II.C (artikel 91a, eerste en tweede lid Wfsv)
NZa decision to let Wlz spending stand as lawful spending
NZa may change an irrevocable regional budget decision
NZa sets acceptable costs for providers via policy rules
p: The NZa may decide to let Wlz spending that falls outside the statutory package stand as lawful spending, shifting spending decisions from statute to regulator discretion, capped at one percent of the budget.
Appeal against regional budget decisions is channelled directly to the court and bars objection, and such decisions become irrevocable unless the NZa changes them, narrowing routes for challenge.
The minister may fix budget frameworks for up to five future years by ministerial regulation without further parliamentary approval, with earmarking allowed.

parties: Asks whether the extra care office role makes the system more complex and whether the care offices can be trusted with the added task; asks about arbitrariness in implementation.
Does this extra link not make the care system more complicated and complex?
Wordt het zorgstelsel met deze extra schakel niet juist ingewikkelder en complexer?
Supports the aims but questions effectiveness, how preventive budgets are funded, and whether all parties should contribute proportionately.
They still have a number of questions about the effectiveness of the bill and whether the stated problems will actually be solved.</evidence_en>
Zij hebben nog wel een aantal vragen over de effectiviteit van het wetsvoorstel en of genoemde problemen daadwerkelijk worden opgelost.
Supports cross-domain prevention but worries that the optional nature of investment could create large regional differences and asks how the government will monitor it.
They note there are concerns this could lead to large regional differences, with one region investing in prevention and another not.
Zij merken op dat er zorgen zijn dat dit kan leiden tot grote regionale verschillen, waarin de ene regio wel investeert in preventie en de andere niet.
Sceptical that adding care offices as a preventive financier reduces fragmentation or costs; asks about shifting of responsibilities between parties and about arbitrariness.
These members see the risk that these legislative changes make care even more expensive, fragmented and complex.
Deze leden zien het risico dat deze wetswijzigingen de zorg nog duurder, gefragmenteerder en complexer maakt.
Asks how care offices will be motivated to take preventive measures, the cap on amounts, and how effectiveness and proposed measures are assessed.
However, the amendment contains no obligation or incentive for the care offices to actually take the preventive measures.
Echter, in de wijziging is geen verplichting of stimulans opgenomen dat de zorgkantoren de preventieve maatregelen ook daadwerkelijk zullen nemen.
Argues the bill reduces incentives for municipalities and insurers to invest in prevention and asks how partnership and financial incentives can be made to work.
The bill creates openings whereby municipalities and health insurers have less incentive for prevention, the BBB members observe.
Het wetsvoorstel creëert openingen waardoor er voor gemeenten en zorgverzekeraars juist minder aansporing ligt voor preventie, zo constateren de leden van de BBB-fractie.
Asks about the Raad van State's point that the bill removes obstacles but does not automatically produce cooperation, how willekeur will be prevented, and requests the AMvB before plenary.
How does the government want to prevent arbitrariness?
Hoe wil de regering willekeur voorkomen?

Criticises the lack of a careful weighing of disadvantages, questions the complexity of a separate funding stream, and asks whether a multi-year financial frame limits budget adjustment and the Tweede Kamer's budget right.
The SP members first of all miss a careful weighing in the explanatory memorandum, which also includes the possible disadvantages of the bill.
De leden van de SP-fractie missen allereerst een zorgvuldige afweging in de memorie van toelichting, waarin ook de mogelijke nadelen van het wetsvoorstel worden meegenomen.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a bill allowing care offices to fund cross-domain prevention from the Long-term Care Fund and enabling multi-year contracting, noting effectiveness doubts about cross-domain cooperation given cost-shifting incentives and the need to preserve flexibility in multi-year budgets. The minister's reply adds sections on effectiveness and feasibility and on maintaining flexibility, and makes further technical adjustments.
concerns: The Afdeling doubts that the broadened funding powers will actually produce cross-domain cooperation, since financial incentives still encourage cost-shifting between care and municipal domains.
The Afdeling asks for explanation of what kind of care the prevention measures target and where the workforce will come from, and the reply adds an effectiveness and feasibility section.

The Afdeling asks for a weighing of the desire for budget certainty and savings against the need for flexibility to adjust multi-year budgets to cuts or new insights, and the reply adds a section on preserving flexibility.

36495.s: The bill implements the EU Digital Markets Act in the Netherlands by designating the Autoriteit Consument en Markt (ACM) as the national authority empowered to investigate possible non-compliance with Articles 5, 6 and 7 on its own initiative, and to assist European Commission inspections. It also amends the Code of Civil Procedure and the General Administrative Law Act to govern cooperation between the Commission and national civil courts.
36495.j: The memorandum justifies the ACM's own-initiative investigative powers by the need for an accessible, effective national authority with specialist knowledge and capacity to support Commission enforcement.
q: With this bill, the Autoriteit Consument en Markt (hereafter: the ACM) is designated as the competent national authority in the Netherlands.
Met dit wetsvoorstel wordt de Autoriteit Consument en Markt (hierna: de ACM) aangewezen als de bevoegde nationale autoriteit in Nederland.
p: Gives the ACM competence to investigate possible non-compliance with the DMA on its own initiative, while excluding certain Instellingswet powers from applying to this task.
Allows ACM officials to assist Commission inspections, including use of the sterke arm (police or equivalent) against resistance, subject to an existing legal framework for such force.

parties: Asks which other member states will use the ACM's discretionary power to start own investigations and whether the sanctions are not too severe for gatekeepers.
These members note that this power in the regulation under Article 38(7) is to be seen as optional.
Deze leden constateren dat deze bevoegdheid in de verordening onder het zevende lid van artikel 38 als optioneel dient te worden gezien.
Supports the regulation as a necessary intervention and asks about rights of small businesses to report gatekeepers, privacy safeguards and coordination between regulators.
These members see the European regulation as a necessary and robust intervention in the digital market.
Deze leden zien de Europese verordening als een noodzakelijke en stevige ingreep op de digitale markt.
Asks whether the ACM has sufficient enforcement capacity, the criteria for launching investigations, and how consumer data is protected during lengthy designation procedures.
These members ask how it is ensured that the ACM has sufficient supervisory capacity.
Deze leden vragen hoe ervoor wordt gezorgd dat de ACM voldoende toezichtcapaciteit heeft.
Asks how national and EU regulators coordinate where enforcement overlaps, and whether an ACM investigation can continue on other laws after the Commission opens its own case.
These members ask how strong cooperation can be guaranteed between national supervisors on overlapping digital legislation.
Deze leden vragen hoe een sterke samenwerking gewaarborgd kan worden tussen de nationale toezichthouders.

Asks about the process for designating gatekeepers, the role given to national authorities compared with the Netherlands' goal, and the risk that the Commission is overwhelmed by national investigations.
The D66 members ask how the government assesses the risk that the European Commission will be overwhelmed with investigations carried out by national authorities such as the ACM.
De leden van de D66-fractie vragen hoe de regering het risico inschat dat de Europese Commissie zal worden overstelpt met onderzoeken die zijn uitgevoerd door nationale autoriteiten zoals de ACM.
Questions the feasibility of the six-month compliance deadline for gatekeepers, the vagueness of the 'specific choice' consent concept, and the financial burden of data portability.
Is this a realistic and feasible obligation?
Is dit een realistische en haalbare verplichting?

Supports designating the ACM as national supervisor, asks how EU-level supervision is organised and resourced, and asks whether Apple's changes comply and what powers the ACM has over non-Dutch gatekeepers.
These members ask whether the ACM has any role in supervision at all or whether this is the exclusive competence of the European Commission.
Deze leden vragen of de ACM dan überhaupt een rol heeft in het toezicht of dat dit de exclusieve bevoegdheid is van de Europese Commissie.

Welcomes tackling monopoly positions of large platforms but asks whether the regulation suffices, whether national gatekeepers can be designated by the ACM, and whether the government will share the list of designated platforms with parliament.
Is there a possibility to give the ACM the power to designate gatekeepers at national level?
Bestaat er een mogelijkheid om de ACM de macht te geven poortwachters op nationaal niveau aan te wijzen.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division advised, in its opinion of 18 October 2023, that the explanatory memorandum to the Dutch DMA implementation bill should further address overlap between Commission powers under the Digital Markets Act and ACM powers under general competition law, ne bis in idem, and the relationship with the GDPR and cooperation with the Dutch data protection authority. The minister's reply of 26 January 2024 reports that the explanatory memorandum was expanded in the indicated sections and explains coordination, ne bis in idem case law, and ACM–AP cooperation.
concerns: The Council asked the explanatory memorandum to clarify the overlap between Commission enforcement under the DMA and ACM investigations under general competition law, which the government addressed by expanding sections 4.2.5, 4.2.7 and 7.3.3.

The Council asked how ne bis in idem is guaranteed when different punitive measures may be imposed for the same facts, and the reply explains coordination and recent CJEU case law but leaves final assessment to the courts.

The Council asked the memorandum to address the relationship between the DMA and the GDPR and the consistent interpretation of overlapping norms with the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, which the government addressed by expanding sections 3.7.4, 4.2.6 and 4.2.7.

The Council noted unclarity on how ACM handles complaints and signals about compliance under the various frameworks, and the government explains a single central complaints desk but the Council's point on the High Level Group's role is only partly resolved.

36549.s: The bill creates binding post-office rules for former ministers and state secretaries: a two-year duty to request advice from the advisory college on any paid post, a two-year ban on taking jobs at their former ministry and on certain contacts with civil servants, with exemptions granted by the relevant minister. It also amends the pension law and the advisory college's statute so that a negative advice bars a post from counting as suitable work and gives the college an advisory and publication role.
36549.j: The memorandum justifies the new rules by GRECO and European Commission recommendations on conflicts of interest after ministers leave office, and explains that exemptions are needed for exceptional cases such as official delegations abroad.
q: This bill therefore contains the basis for setting, by or pursuant to a general administrative order, further rules on the procedure for the request for advice.
Dit wetsvoorstel bevat daarom de grondslag om bij of krachtens een algemene maatregel van bestuur nadere regels te stellen over de procedure rondom de adviesaanvraag.
d: procedure for advice requests and data to be supplied
retention period for submitted personal data
exemption from the ban on employment at former ministry
exemption from the lobbying ban on contacts with civil servants
p: The responsible minister may grant exemptions from the employment and lobbying bans, with publication in the Staatscourant as the only safeguard.
Documents on advice requests are kept non-public and challenges to advice are routed only through civil actions, not administrative appeal.

parties: Asks how the advisory committee's time limits would be met and how acceptability of post-office roles is weighed, seeking clarity and uniform guidelines to avoid arbitrariness.
They further ask the government to clarify the advice 'acceptable under conditions'.
Verder vragen zij de regering om een verduidelijking van het advies «aanvaardbaar onder voorwaarden».
Argues the absence of an enforcement and sanctions mechanism risks former ministers ignoring the advisory committee's advice without consequence, and questions reliance on naming-and-shaming.
This approach of the bill carries the serious risk that no action can be taken against former ministers who ignore the advice of the advisory committee.

Deze insteek van het wetsvoorstel brengt het zwaarwegende risico met zich mee dat er niet opgetreden kan worden tegen gewezen bewindspersonen die het advies van het Adviescollege rechtspositie politieke ambtsdragers (hierna:

Objects that the ministry secretary-general, a subordinate with a close relationship, would decide exemptions, and asks why the advisory body's advice is not mandatory or binding and why the lobbying ban excludes sitting ministers.
That this very person should decide on a possible exception, these members find a remarkable and unwise choice.
Dat uitgerekend deze persoon zou moeten beslissen over een eventuele uitzondering vinden deze leden een opmerkelijke en onverstandige keuze.
Says the bill is too weak, criticises the minister's discretion to grant lobbying-ban exemptions as subjective and prone to pressure, and asks for sanctions and an independent commission.
These members think it is wrong that this adds a degree of subjectivity.
Deze leden vinden het verkeerd dat hiermee een mate van subjectiviteit wordt toegevoegd hierdoor.
Asks about the legal consequences of the mandatory advice, such as use in tort claims by third parties, and whether the bill clarifies its scope in advance.
These members ask the government to reflect on what the status of the legally mandatory advice, and also of not requesting it, could be if citizens brought legal actions.
Deze leden vragen de regering om een reflectie wat de status van het wettelijk verplichte advies, en bijvoorbeeld ook het niet vragen ervan, kan zijn als burgers juridische acties zouden instellen.
Asks how the advisory committee can advise carefully under time pressure, how it avoids definitional disputes, and why an exemption request is optional rather than mandatory.
These members ask the government to explain why a discretionary provision was chosen and why an advice request is not mandatory when granting an exemption.
Deze leden vragen de regering nader toe te lichten waarom hier gekozen is voor een kan-bepaling en waarom bij het verlenen van een ontheffing een adviesaanvraag niet als verplichting is gesteld.

Questions the non-binding nature of the advice, the omission of sanctions, and the gap that lets the ban not apply to sitting ministers and non-adjacent ministries, and asks why political assistants are excluded.
The ban now applies to a prohibition between former ministers and civil servants.
Het verbod ziet nu op een verbod tussen oud-bewindspersonen en ambtenaren.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on a draft bill regulating post-office careers of former ministers and state secretaries (cooling-off period, advisory obligation, revolving-door and lobbying bans), raising principled objections about juridisation, the public/semi-public carve-out, legal certainty of norms, legal protection and the workability of the Arpa advisory body. The minister's reply largely rejects the proposal to route advice through the Minister-President and to reconsider the advisory obligation, but accepts extending the scope to all sectors, clarifying criteria, adding hearing rights and the Arpa workload points.
concerns: The Afdeling said the advice given directly to former ministers leaves no ministerial responsibility to parliament and advised routing advice via the Minister-President, which the government declined.

The Afdeling warned the advisory obligation may be counterproductive through juridisation and that the bill must be embedded in a broader integrity policy; the government defended the measure but added integrity-policy context.

The Afdeling found the material standard (risk of conflict of interest, 'intensive' involvement in policy fields) unclear and the terminology inconsistent; the government revised the criteria and wording.

The Afdeling advised extending the advisory and lobbying rules beyond the private and part of the semi-public sector, since conflicts of interest also arise in public and semi-public domains; the government accepted and removed the sector distinction.
The Afdeling acknowledged the bans restrict free choice of work and privacy but found them justified and proportionate given their temporary two-year duration.

The Afdeling noted that civil-court remedies are unrealistic in practice and asked for stronger procedural safeguards; the government added a hearing right for negative and conditional advice and an explicit extension period but kept the civil-law route.
