The Afdeling questioned whether the Arpa can handle individual cases in short time frames given its advisory mandate and expertise; the government agreed to discuss workload, procedures and resources with the Arpa.
The Afdeling asked for a fuller explanation of the bill's effect on the attractiveness of ministerial posts and its coherence with other remuneration rules; the government added explanatory text.

36550-III.s: This supplementary budget bill amends the 2024 budget statements for the Ministry of General Affairs, the Cabinet of the King, the Oversight Committee on the Intelligence and Security Services, and the related agency, with increases in spending and a retroactive effective date of 1 June 2024. It contains no delegation of rule-making power or changes to oversight mechanisms.
q: Amendment of the departmental budget statement of the Ministry of General Affairs (IIIA), the budget statement of the Cabinet of the King (IIIB), and the budget statement of the Oversight Committee on the Intelligence and Security Services (IIIC).

Wijziging van de departementale begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Algemene Zaken (IIIA), de begrotingsstaat van het Kabinet van de Koning (IIIB), de begrotingsstaat van de Commissie van Toezicht op de Inlichtingen- en Veiligheidsdiensten (IIIC)

36558.s: The bill lets municipal councils, provincial states, water boards, joint-arrangement bodies and Caribbean island councils meet electronically in exceptional circumstances, with public live broadcast and restrictions on certain agenda items. It also allows a three-year experiment with hybrid meetings by general administrative order, subject to four-week parliamentary pre-submission and an evaluation report to parliament.
36558.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by saying that hybrid meetings' effects must be studied by experiment and that a general administrative order is needed to set comparable conditions, with parliamentary involvement and evaluation.
q: The bill further continues to guarantee that deliberation and decision-making can be followed by the public (remotely).
Het wetsvoorstel blijft daarnaast garanderen dat de beraadslaging en besluitvorming voor het publiek (op afstand) te volgen is.
d: technical requirements for the electronic meeting environment
experiment allowing hybrid council meetings for up to three years in designated bodies
p: Allows a ministerial-designated experiment with hybrid meetings via general administrative order, with four-week parliamentary pre-submission, an evaluation report to parliament, a three-year limit and early termination by the minister.

Allows councils to meet electronically in exceptional circumstances, with live public broadcast and exclusions for appointments and oath-taking, leaving the judgement of exceptional circumstances to the council itself.

parties: Worries that shifting from physical to digital meetings reduces openness and transparency of decision-making by councils and joint-arrangement boards, and asks how the definition of exceptional circumstances will be monitored.
Can the government also indicate how it is monitored that the definition is not interpreted more broadly by provincial states, municipal councils, island councils and general boards?
Kan de regering ook aangeven op welke wijze gemonitord wordt dat de definitie door provinciale staten, gemeenteraden, eilandraden en algemene besturen niet breder wordt geïnterpreteerd?
Asks whether the broad scope could make digital meetings the norm and create large differences between municipalities, and how identification will be secured against deepfakes.
By leaving room for local considerations, large differences between municipalities may arise.],
Door in dezen ruimte te laten voor lokale afwegingen kunnen er grote verschillen tussen gemeenten ontstaan.
Asks for criteria to fill in 'exceptional circumstances', safeguards against politicised choice of meeting modality, and minority remedies against majority decisions.
What options do minority factions have to contest the majority's decision?
Welke mogelijkheden hebben minderheidsfracties om de beslissing van de meerderheid aan te vechten?
Asks how minorities are protected from being sidelined by a majority choosing digital meetings and how free, independent voting is guaranteed during digital sessions.
How is it guaranteed that council members can speak and vote freely and independently during digital meetings?
Op welke manier wordt gewaarborgd dat raadsleden vrij en onafhankelijk kunnen spreken en stemmen tijdens digitale vergaderingen

Finds the 'exceptional circumstances' criterion too open-ended, wants it tied to calamities and actual obstruction, and asks why municipalities are not obliged to fix in their rules when digital meetings apply; also questions the constitutional basis of digital assembly.
These members ask why the bill, given its importance, does not expressly require municipalities to record in which situations digital meetings may apply.
Deze leden vragen waarom het wetsvoorstel, gelet op het belang ervan, niet uitdrukkelijk bepaalt dat gemeenten vastleggen in welke situaties digitaal vergaderen aan de orde kan zijn.

Strongly opposes making digital meetings permanent and leaving their scope to councils, arguing it undermines the constitutional value of physical assembly and invites the Council of State's objection to be ignored.
These members are very critical of this bill because it disregards the importance of physical meetings by elected representatives for a full democratic process.
Deze leden zijn zeer kritisch op voorliggend wetsvoorstel omdat het wetsvoorstel het belang miskent van fysiek vergaderen door volksvertegenwoordigers voor een volwaardig democratisch proces.

Asks how the bill addresses barriers for citizens and councillors without good internet or digital skills, and how the evaluation's recommendations on transparency and journalist access are implemented.
To what extent does the government, in this legislation, take account of these digital barriers?
In hoeverre heeft de regering in deze wetgeving oog voor deze digitale barrières?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the bill allowing generic digital council meetings for decentralised bodies was constitutionally and policy-wise problematic, that physical meetings must remain the statutory norm, and that digital meetings should be limited to legally defined emergencies and purely internal matters, with the hybrid experiment similarly restricted. The government reply largely accepts this, restoring physical meetings as the main rule and tightening the bill and explanatory memorandum, while still opposing a statutory list of emergency situations and arguing constitutional openness.
concerns: The Afdeling argued that openness and the constitutional role of the physical council hall preclude treating digital and physical meetings as equivalent, while the government maintains there are no constitutional obstacles but accepts physical meetings as the main rule.

The Afdeling advised limiting digital meetings to statutorily defined emergencies and purely internal matters; the government declined to specify emergency situations in statute, relying on decentralised prudence.

The Afdeling advised that the choice between physical and digital meetings should not be left to local autonomy but set by the legislator; the government accepted a legal norm of physical meetings as main rule but kept a generic option for councils.

The Afdeling noted that under the disability convention the priority is removing physical barriers rather than offering a digital alternative; the government agreed barriers should be removed but maintained that hybrid meetings also aid accessibility.
The Afdeling noted that the bill's cross-reference makes digital-meeting consequences apply to committees without the enabling provision; the government agreed to adjust the wording.

The Afdeling said the explanatory memorandum gave an incomplete picture of support for digital meetings; the government agreed to correct the description, including the Statenlid NU consultation reply.

36576.s: The bill establishes a legal framework for collective heat supply (warmtenetten) to secure reliable, affordable and greenhouse-gas-free heating, giving municipalities (college van B&W) power to define heat zones (warmtekavels) and appoint a single heat company with exclusive rights and public-service obligations. It also sets ACM tariff regulation, supervision, emergency intervention powers and transitional rules for a seven-year ingroeiperiode allowing non-public heat companies.
36576.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations and new municipal powers by the need for municipalities to steer the heat transition and by the difficulty of enforcing public interests through regulation alone.
d: further rules on grounds and notification for heat zones
deadline for public-majority heat company to declare intention
rules on application, grounds, global zone plan and conditions for designation
rules on ranking criteria and conditions for designation during ingroeiperiode
further rules on heat company tasks
rules on investment plan and contingency supply sources
emission norms for collective heat supply
procedure for withdrawing a designation and selecting another heat company
p: Municipal executives gain power to define heat zones and designate exclusive heat companies, with provincial written views as the only check and limited scope for public scrutiny.
ACM may order third parties to supply heat, appoint a silent administrator and replace a heat company's board when supply security is at risk, with limited judicial safeguards in the text shown.

parties: Questions the effectiveness, legal compatibility with EU law, cost and delay consequences of the mandatory public majority stake and asks for government guarantees and cost information.
Can the government guarantee the House that the bill does not conflict with European legislation?
Kan de regering de Kamer garanderen dat het wetsvoorstel niet in strijd is met Europese wetgeving?
Supports the need for the bill but asks for expected connection figures and experience with existing public and private heat companies.
The D66 members ask the government for figures on how many or what share of existing heat networks are owned by a (partly) public heat company and how many by private ones.

De leden van de D66-fractie vragen de regering cijfers te geven over hoeveel of welk aandeel van de nu bestaande warmtenetten in handen zijn van een (deels) publiek warmtebedrijf en hoeveel van private warmtebedrijven.
Questions whether the cost-based tariff system with a tariff cap and equalisation fund still yields transparent tariffs and how public ownership safeguards citizens' interests.
Supports public energy infrastructure in principle but doubts the mandatory public majority is justified and asks for evidence and consideration of less intrusive alternatives.
On the other hand, the requirement is very far-reaching for heat companies and currently brings a great deal of uncertainty for the parties involved.
Anderzijds is het genoemde vereiste zeer ingrijpend voor warmtebedrijven en gaat het momenteel gepaard met veel onzekerheid voor betrokken partijen.
Accepts the case for public majority ownership but asks how democratic control and local steering hold up when companies operate at regional scale and municipalities lack capacity.
What does this mean, however, for democratic control and the degree of local steering?
Wat betekent dit echter voor de democratische controle en de mate van lokale sturing?
Sees heat networks as important for a climate-neutral future and urges swift treatment of the bill to give clarity to parties.
They hope for a swift treatment of the bill that provides clarity so that the parties involved know where they stand.
Zij hopen op een spoedige behandeling van de wet die duidelijkheid biedt zodat betrokken partijen weten waar zij aan toe zijn.
Asks for criteria defining affordable heat, what recourse households have against higher tariffs, and how municipal designation powers would be limited.
The NSC members ask what right a household has to refuse the new tariff if it is higher than the current tariff linked to the gas price.
De leden van de NSC-fractie vragen welk recht een huishouden heeft om het nieuwe tarief te weigeren als dit meer is dan het huidige tarief dat gekoppeld is aan de gasprijs.

v.summary: The Council of State advisory division accepts the policy aim of the Dutch heat bill (Wet collectieve warmte) but raises objections to the required public majority ownership of heat companies, to the justification for tariff regulation and affordability, and asks for statutory emissions norms. The government's reply (nader rapport) defends the public majority requirement, adds reasoning and reference to legal advice, and partly accepts the remarks on tariff affordability and financial risks.
concerns: The Afdeling finds insufficient justification that a mandatory public majority stake is necessary, given less intrusive regulatory alternatives such as a selection procedure or municipal self-provision.
The public majority requirement touches free movement of capital and freedom of establishment and must be justified and proportionate under EU law.
Interference with the property right of existing heat companies requires a fair balance and examination of less intrusive alternatives, which the explanatory memorandum does not sufficiently show.
Tariff regulation shifting to cost-based tariffs raises affordability and social acceptability questions that the explanatory memorandum does not adequately address.
The explanatory memorandum should explain financial risks for public shareholders, state aid compliance, and the diversity of public shareholder interests.
Greater attention is needed to the interests of (future) consumers in decisions on new heat networks and the financial effects of the new tariff regime.

36585.s: The bill amends the Dutch Criminal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure so that a court or prosecutor may require, as a special condition, that a person subject to an alcohol ban be monitored with an Alcoholmeter (a transdermal ankle-band alcohol sensor), in addition to blood or urine tests. The bill does not change who decides to impose an alcohol ban, and the explanatory memorandum argues the device is a proportionate, legally grounded monitoring tool.
36585.j: The memorandum justifies the new monitoring option by pilot results showing fewer offences and better supervision of alcohol bans, and argues it is a less intrusive alternative to frequent urine tests, subject to proportionality and necessity review by the court or prosecutor.
q: With this bill the necessary statutory basis is provided for the use of the Alcoholmeter as a monitoring tool.
Met dit wetsvoorstel wordt voorzien in de daarvoor noodzakelijke wettelijke grondslag.
p: Adds a statutory basis for continuous transdermal alcohol monitoring as a special condition, expanding the monitoring options available to the court or prosecutor and reducing the privacy protection of convicted or suspected persons, with the memorandum requiring case-by-case necessity and proportionality assessment.

parties: Asks about effectiveness of the ankle alcohol meter, the pilot's representativeness and the capacity needed from reclassering and police.
These members ask the government to explain how one can speak of a successful pilot when only 25 people participated and those who volunteered are likely not the problem group.

Effecten op het drinkgedrag De leden van de PVV-fractie vragen of de regering kan uitleggen hoe je van een succesvolle pilot kan spreken als er maar 25 mensen meedoen en degenen die vrijwillig meedoen in hoge mate van waarschijnlijk niet de probleemgroep vormen.
Questions whether the meter is effective given it detected alcohol use in only 29 percent of cases, and asks whether judges can impose it alongside drug bans.
Does this mean that in 71 percent of cases where someone used alcohol, the alcohol meter did not detect it?
Betekent dit dat in 71 procent van de gevallen dat iemand alcohol heeft gebruikt de alcoholmeter dat niet detecteerde?
Supports the meter but asks about cost recovery, workload at DV&O, and whether the Raad voor de rechtspraak's advice on mandatory cooperation was followed.

The VVD members support the possibility of using the alcohol meter as a means to check whether a suspect or convicted person complies with an imposed alcohol ban and wish to raise some further questions and remarks.

Deze leden ondersteunen de mogelijkheid om de alcoholmeter in te zetten als middel om te controleren of een verdachte of veroordeelde zich aan een opgelegd alcoholverbod houdt en wensen hierover nog enkele vragen/opmerkingen te maken.
Warns that using the meter on minors and young adults may be more burdensome and infringe freedom of movement and personal integrity, and asks for evaluation first.
According to these members, this restriction of the right to freedom of movement and infringement on personal integrity may be worse for minors and young adults than for adults.
Deze beperking van het recht op bewegingsvrijheid en inbreuk op de persoonlijke integriteit kan volgens de leden bij jeugdigen en jongvolwassenen erger zijn dan bij volwassenen.
Argues the measure seriously infringes fundamental rights, that its benefits look limited against these burdens, and asks for stronger justification of necessity and effectiveness.
Imposing the obligation to wear an alcohol meter is after all a serious infringement on fundamental rights.
Het verplicht opleggen van het dragen van een alcoholmeter vormt immers een serieuze inbreuk op grondrechten.
Concerned about reliability (false negatives), discomfort causing bruising, the non-voluntary nature and unclear sanctions for refusal.
They read that an important aspect of this law is the no longer voluntary nature of the alcohol meter, so it can be imposed involuntarily.
Zij lezen dat een belangrijk aspect van deze wet zit in het niet meer vrijwillige karakter van de alcoholmeter en dat deze dus onvrijwillig kan worden opgelegd.
Sees effectiveness and time savings but asks how objections of the suspect are weighed by reclassering and whether a sanction applies to tampering.
Can the government go deeper into the grounds on which the reclassering decides whether the alcohol meter is deployed?
Kan de regering dieper ingaan op de gronden waarop de reclassering beslist of de alcoholmeter wordt ingezet?
Asks whether fraud with the meter can be excluded and whether the alcohol lock becomes unnecessary when the meter is worn, citing the Openbaar Ministerie's advice.
These members ask the government to what extent the possibilities for fraud with the alcohol meter have been examined.
Deze leden vragen de regering in hoeverre de mogelijkheden tot fraude aan de alcoholmeter onderzocht zijn.
Asks whether offenders should be allowed to choose between the alcohol meter and the older urine-check method, given infringements on fundamental rights.

In light of the, whether or not justified, infringement on some fundamental rights, has consideration been given to letting convicted persons choose between the old method of checking and the proposed method with an alcohol meter.

vragen naar aanleiding van de, al dan niet terechte, inbreuk op enkele grondrechten of is overwegen om veroordeelden die een alcoholverbod opgelegd hebben gekregen te laten kiezen tussen de oude manier van controleren en de voorgestelde wijze, met een alcoholmeter.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft bill introducing an alcohol monitoring ankle device (alcoholmeter) to supervise alcohol bans, raising concerns about effectiveness, intrusion on privacy, bodily integrity and freedom of movement, minors, legal protection and data transfer to the US. The minister's reply largely adopted the advice by expanding justification, adding legal protection discussion, clarifying data processing and updating the EU-US data framework analysis.
concerns: The Afdeling found the claimed effectiveness of the alcoholmeter insufficiently substantiated given small pilots and lack of long-term evidence, and the government expanded the justification.

The Afdeling considered the continuous monitoring a greater intrusion on privacy, bodily integrity and freedom of movement than urine checks, requiring a stronger proportionality and subsidiarity assessment, which the government added.

The Afdeling advised assessing the restriction of freedom of movement under Article 2 of Protocol 4 ECHR and addressing legal protection for the wearer after monitoring starts, which the government incorporated.
The Afdeling asked for justification of the use of the alcoholmeter on minors, which the government addressed by explaining the existing legal framework and need for case-by-case assessment.

The Afdeling required a fuller assessment of personal data protection under Article 10 Constitution, Articles 7 and 8 EU Charter and Article 8 ECHR, which the government added to the data protection impact assessment.

The Afdeling asked for updated grounds for transfer of data to SCRAM in the US and clarification of the Schrems II implications, which the government addressed by describing the Data Privacy Framework and standard contract while SCRAM certification was still pending.
The Afdeling asked for clarification of the data processing chain, SCRAM's role as processor or controller, and retention periods, which the government clarified in the explanatory memorandum.

36600-IV.s: This bill sets the 2025 budget statements for Koninkrijksrelaties (IV) and the BES-fonds (H) in one law, as the Comptabiliteitswet 2016 permits. The explanatory memorandum sets out 2025 priorities for Caribbean Netherlands (good governance, border supervision, public finances, self-reliance) and the budgetary effects of policy.
36600-IV.j: The memorandum justifies the budget through the Comptabiliteitswet 2016 framework and the stated policy priorities for Caribbean Netherlands, without justifying any new delegation of power.
q: The budget statements that form part of the national budget are each established separately by law under article 2.3, first paragraph, of the Comptabiliteitswet 2016.
De begrotingsstaten die onderdeel zijn van de Rijksbegroting, worden op grond van artikel 2.3, eerste lid, van de Comptabiliteitswet 2016 elk afzonderlijk bij de wet vastgesteld.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State issued a blanco advice (no remarks) on the 2025 budget bill for Kingdom Relations and the BES fund, advising submission to the Tweede Kamer. The government's nader rapport confirms this and reports minor technical adjustments to the budget (augustusbesluitvorming in article 4, with no change to total expenditure or revenue).

36600-VI.s: This is the 2025 budget bill for the Ministry of Justice and Security, setting the departmental budget statement (Art. 31-38, 91-93) and the budget of six business-unit agencies (DJI, CJIB, NFI, Justis, Justid, JIO) in thousands of euros. It also states the Minister is not responsible for the efficiency of judicial organisation operations, consistent with judicial self-management under the Wet op de rechterlijke organisatie.
q: Referring to article 4.1 of the Comptabiliteitswet 2016 in conjunction with articles 23 and 91 of the Wet op de rechterlijke organisatie, the Minister is not responsible for the efficiency of the judiciary's business operations.

Onder verwijzing naar artikel 4.1 van de Comptabiliteitswet 2016 jo. de artikelen 23 en 91 van de Wet op de rechterlijke organisatie is Onze Minister niet verantwoordelijk voor de doelmatigheid van de bedrijfsvoering van de rechterlijke organisatie.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering has no remarks on the 2025 budget bill for the Ministry of Justice and Security and advises submitting it to the Tweede Kamer. The Minister of Finance's reply notes that several budgets need amendments and attaches these as annexes.

36613-III.s: This bill amends the 2024 budget statements of the Ministry of General Affairs, the Cabinet of the King and the Commission for Oversight of the Intelligence and Security Services, mainly by small reallocations and a supplementary budget increase. It does not delegate rule-making power or shift powers between the executive and checking institutions.
q: Amended, as shown in the corresponding budget statement attached to this law.
Gewijzigd, zoals blijkt uit de desbetreffende bij deze wet behorende staat.

36625-X.s: This bill amends the 2024 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Defence (second supplementary budget), adjusting commitment, expenditure and revenue appropriations across operational and non-operational articles. The main drivers are funding for reservist leave back-pay following a court ruling, increased reservist costs, and budget transfers including to COMMIT.
36625-X.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies the budget changes by a court ruling requiring retroactive payment of reservist leave and by rising reservist numbers, and describes the transfer to COMMIT as technical in nature.
q: As a result of a court ruling, Defence will pay out reservists' leave retroactively for 5 years.
Defensie zal als gevolg van een rechterlijke uitspraak het verlof van reservisten met terugwerkende kracht voor 5 jaar uitbetalen.

36639.s: The bill introduces the citizen service number (BSN) and digital government facilities in the public bodies Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba by amending the BSN, basic personal data administration, population registration and digital government acts. It extends registration, oversight, data-quality audits and information duties to Caribbean Netherlands and sets out how the Minister and public bodies will supervise and share data.
36639.j: The explanatory memorandum justifies the delegations by the need for technical detail and for consistent data quality across registers, and argues that existing appeal and supervision rights continue to apply.
q: For the rules that apply in full to Caribbean Netherlands, the explanatory memorandum to the Wdo is referred to for substantive explanation.
Voor de regels die onverkort voor Caribisch Nederland komen te gelden, wordt voor een inhoudelijke toelichting verwezen naar de memorie van toelichting bij Wdo.
d: ARTIKEL II, G (artikel 30a, derde lid Wet bap BES)
periodicity and execution of audits and content of excerpts
special grant to public bodies for digital transition
ARTIKEL III, I (artikel 2.82-2.86 Wet BRP, algemene maatregel van bestuur referenced in 2.82(3)(b))
additional data recorded for residents of public bodies
p: Gives the Minister a legal power to periodically compare and check data across the population registers, with notification duties to municipal or public-body authorities.
ARTIKEL II, C (artikel 12a Wet bap BES) and ARTIKEL V (Wet digitale overheid Chapter 7a)
Extends registration and digital authentication obligations to Caribbean Netherlands, while preserving appeal rights under the administrative justice act for registration decisions.

parties: Asks how personal data protection is guaranteed under dual registration, how data discrepancies are handled, and how the AP and CBP BES split supervision.
In this situation, how is the protection of personal data guaranteed?
Hoe is in deze situatie de bescherming van de persoonsgegevens gegarandeerd?
Supports improving digital government services in the Caribbean Netherlands and has no additional questions.

These members endorse the importance of improving digital government services in the Caribbean Netherlands and welcome the aim of bringing them to an equivalent level with the European part of the Netherlands.

Deze leden onderschrijven het belang van het verbeteren van de digitale overheidsdienstverlening in Caribisch Nederland en juichen de inzet toe om deze op een gelijkwaardig niveau te brengen met het Europese deel van Nederland.
Has no further questions at this stage.
These members currently have no further questions.
Deze leden hebben op dit moment geen nadere vragen.
Asks whether island authorities have sufficient capacity to prevent and address misuse of the BSN, and how misuse is monitored.
How is it monitored to what extent a BSN will be used in cases of misuse of government provisions?
Op welke manier wordt gemonitord in hoeverre een BSN gebruikt zal worden bij misbruik van overheidsvoorzieningen?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised on the bill introducing the BSN and digital government facilities in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, raising remarks on side effects, the constitutional and ECHR justification, data transfer safeguards and phased entry into force, and asked for the explanatory memorandum to be supplemented. The government's nader rapport reports that the explanatory memorandum was extended on each point and the bill technically amended, largely following the advice.
concerns: The explanatory memorandum's justification under Article 10 of the Constitution and Article 8 ECHR (necessity, proportionality, data protection principles) was insufficiently precise and was expanded.

Adequate safeguards for transfers of personal data from Europe to Caribbean Netherlands were insufficiently explained; the government added organisational measures and clarified the consensus statute's relevance, while the Afdeling's point on training and awareness is only partly met.
Possible side effects of the BSN, such as identity fraud and networking risks, were not discussed; the explanatory memorandum now addresses them and the BSN was removed from the ID card BES.
The bill lacked a planned entry-into-force date and justification for differentiated commencement; a phased timetable targeting 2025 was added.
Insufficient attention to the citizen perspective on the paper route versus digital alternatives; a new chapter on information, communication and digital skills was added.

36648.s: The bill limits the definition of service costs in the Dutch Civil Code to categories listed in a general administrative order (amvb), and adds ministerial power to set calculation rules and maximum amounts for service costs. It also extends the Huurcommissie's power to set advance service-cost payments and to fix annual statements when landlords fail to provide them.
36648.j: The memorandum justifies the ministerial power to set calculation rules and maximum amounts by the need to adapt quickly to economic realities and to prevent excesses, and the amvb route by the wish for a clear, limitative list.
q: A delegation basis is further proposed under which regulations may be set by ministerial regulation on the method of calculation and the maximum height of service costs.

Voorts wordt een delegatiegrondslag voorgesteld op grond waarvan het mogelijk is om in een ministeriële regeling regels te stellen over de wijze van berekening en de maximale hoogte van de servicekosten.
d: ARTIKEL I, A (Art. 7:237, derde lid BW)
categories of service costs listed in general administrative order
ARTIKEL I, A (Art. 7:237, derde lid BW)
calculation method and maximum height of service costs
ARTIKEL II, I (Art. 18 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
fixed amount for service costs when landlord provides no annual statement
ARTIKEL II, K (Art. 19 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
Huurcommissie may apply a different percentage for advance service-cost payments
p: ARTIKEL I, A (Art. 7:237, derde lid BW)
Service costs are made dependent on an exhaustive list set by general administrative order, with a direct ministerial power to set maximum amounts that can be changed quickly.
ARTIKEL II, K (Art. 19 Uitvoeringswet huurprijzen woonruimte)
The Huurcommissie gains discretion to depart from the statutory CPI percentage when setting advance payments, a power that strengthens an oversight body rather than the executive.

parties: Asks whether municipalities impose fines on landlords and how often, and questions the costs and funding of Huurcommissie disputes.
The PVV members read in the explanatory memorandum that municipalities can impose administrative fines on landlords who violate the rules.
De leden van de PVV-fractie lezen in de memorie van toelichting bij het wetsvoorstel dat gemeenten een bestuurlijke boete kunnen opleggen aan verhuurders die in overtreding zijn.
Wants landlords obliged to report and justify service charges annually with sanctions, and worries that norm amounts set by the Huurcommissie could be chosen over actual costs.
These members find it important that tenants clearly understand how service charges arise and therefore consider it important that landlords properly justify the service charges.

De leden van de GroenLinks-PvdA-fractie vinden het belangrijk dat huurders goed inzicht krijgen in hoe de servicekosten tot stand komen en daarom vinden zij het van belang dat verhuurders de servicekosten goed moeten onderbouwen.
Asks whether the limitative list can be flexibly amended or extended and how it will be communicated.
The VVD members wonder whether the list of service charges can be flexibly expanded so that developments in society can be responded to.
De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen zich af of de lijst van servicekosten flexibel kan worden uitgebreid, zodat ingespeeld kan worden op ontwikkelingen in de samenleving.
Asks how the Huurcommissie sets norm amounts, whether it can set amounts higher than actual costs, and whether parties can object to joint handling of cases.
These members ask the government to what extent these norm amounts correspond to the amounts of an annual statement drawn up by the landlord themselves.
Deze leden vragen de regering in welke mate deze normbedragen overeenkomen met de bedragen van een jaarafrekening opgesteld door de verhuurder zelf.
Asks whether norm amounts create a perverse incentive for landlords to forgo annual statements and how often the lists will be evaluated.
These members wonder why this would be an incentive for landlords to draw up an annual statement.
Deze leden vragen zich af waarom dit een prikkel zou zijn voor verhuurders om een jaarafrekening op te stellen.
Asks about the risks of a limitative list, about possible fines for landlords who do not provide annual statements, and about making annual reporting a legal obligation.
They also ask about including in the law that annual reporting on service charges is an obligation resting on the landlord.
Ook vragen zij naar het opnemen in de wet dat het jaarlijks rapporteren over de servicekosten een verplichting is die rust bij de verhuurder.
Asks why landlords lost nearly all disputes and whether tenants were pressured into optional facility agreements.
These members ask how it came about that in almost 100% of cases the landlord was found to be in the wrong.
De leden van de BBB-fractie vragen hoe het zover gekomen is dat in vrijwel 100% van de zaken de verhuurder in het ongelijk werd gesteld.
Asks why only regulated-sector advance payments can be reviewed by the Huurcommissie and whether landlords will prefer norm amounts over actual statements.
The SP members ask the government why it is only possible to have the advance service charge amount in the regulated rental sector reviewed by the Huurcommissie.
De leden van de SP-fractie vragen de regering waarom het alleen mogelijk is om het voorschotbedrag voor servicekosten in de gereguleerde huursector te laten toetsen door de Huurcommissie.
Asks which items will be in the AMvB, how the list stays up to date for new housing forms, and what framework governs the ministerial regulation.
Can the government already indicate which service charges will or may be included in this AMvB?
Kan de regering reeds aangeven welke servicekosten in deze AMvB worden opgenomen, of mogelijk worden opgenomen?
Asks the government to be restrained in listing items, to set a maximum for non-limitative categories, and to make annual reporting a legal duty; objects that shared-living schemes are not addressed.
The ChristenUnie members ask the government to be restrained in including items or services on the list in the Besluit servicekosten.
De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie vragen de regering terughoudend te zijn in het opnemen van zaken of diensten op de lijst in het Besluit servicekosten.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division reported on a draft bill modernising the system of service charges in Boek 7 BW and related laws, and found no remarks to make, advising that the bill be submitted to the Tweede Kamer. The minister's reply only notes that some redactional changes were made to the explanatory memorandum and forwards the bill.

36657.s: The bill amends the Wet justitiële en strafvorderlijke gegevens to write the purposes for which the Minister may request and consult criminal record data from other EU member states via the European Criminal Records Information System (ECRIS and ECRIS-TCN) into statute, including for integrity screening, adoption, foster care, immigration and nationality decisions. It makes parallel changes to the implementing act for the EU-UK trade agreement and to the Code of Criminal Procedure.
36657.j: The memorandum justifies the new purposes by reference to EU regulation and the proportionality principle, arguing that data use must serve a legitimate, suitable and necessary purpose.
q: As noted in section 2.3 of this explanatory memorandum, the proportionality principle requires that the use of ECRIS serve a legitimate purpose and be suitable and necessary for it.
Zoals in paragraaf 2.3 van deze toelichting geconstateerd, is vanwege het evenredigheidsbeginsel van belang dat het gebruik van Ecris een legitiem doel dient en daartoe geschikt en noodzakelijk is.

parties: Asks for justification of why purposes are only now being codified, how the four purposes were selected, and whether other bodies and oversight agencies should also get Ecris access.

These members ask the government for further justification why it is only now choosing to propose a bill, while this was already required under either the GDPR, the Directive or the Ecris-TCN Regulation.

Deze leden vragen de regering naar een nadere motivering waarom nu pas is gekozen voor een wetsvoorstel, terwijl dat al een vereiste was van ofwel de AVG ofwel de eerdergenoemde richtlijn of de Ecris-TCN-verordening.

Questions the necessity and proportionality of the data processing as a restriction on privacy and data protection, and asks whether the information shared is equivalent across countries and whether individuals are informed when Ecris is consulted.
A restriction may only be imposed if it is necessary and suitable to achieve a legitimate aim.
Een beperking kan slechts worden gesteld indien zij noodzakelijk en geschikt is om een legitiem doel te verwezenlijken.
Accepts the four additional purposes but asks how they were selected and which further purposes other countries have adopted.
These members can agree with these points, but ask how the government arrived at these four additional purposes.
Deze leden kunnen zich vinden in deze punten, maar vragen hoe de regering is gekomen tot deze vier aanvullende doelen.
Asks factual questions on Ecris-TCN timing, whether transmission of conviction information has failed in practice, the UK exchange arrangement, and the financial consequences for different bodies.
These members ask the government whether this is still the expectation and, if so, whether the government can specify when it will be put into use.
Deze leden vragen de regering of dit nog steeds de verwachting is en, zo ja, of de regering meer specifiek kan aangeven wanneer het in gebruik wordt genomen.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises that the explanatory memorandum on the bill setting out the non-criminal purposes of the European Criminal Records Information System (ECRIS and ECRIS-TCN) must be expanded, because the data shared (including parents' names, identity numbers, fingerprints and facial images where available) and the seriousness of the intrusion on privacy and data protection were not adequately described. The government's nader rapport explains which data categories apply under the ECRIS framework decision, states that parents' names, fingerprints and facial images are not processed or exchanged via ECRIS for Dutch authorities, and adds an amendment on the UK cooperation regime but does not fundamentally change the proportionality analysis.
concerns: Processing criminal data is a more than minor intrusion on privacy and data protection, which must be reflected in the necessity and proportionality assessment; the government acknowledges this and clarifies it in the memorandum.

The explanatory memorandum must address which data are shared via ECRIS and assess necessity and proportionality accordingly; the government clarifies the data categories but maintains its existing proportionality framing.
The explanatory memorandum should be supplemented with a description of the data shared via ECRIS, which the government addresses in its reply.

36675.s: The bill creates an unconditional, ex officio compensation scheme for people whose requests for cooperation in an out-of-court debt settlement or stabilisation request were wrongly refused by the Tax Administration, including a flat payment of EUR 500, payment of the debt-repayment capacity amount, and write-off of tax and benefit debts. It also provides for surviving relatives, partners, and an amendment to the General Act on Income-Dependent Schemes to write off benefit debts.
36675.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation in Article 12 as a safeguard to protect fundamental rights when criminal-law data are processed, added on the advice of the Raad van State.
q: Following the advice of the Afdeling, a third paragraph was added to Article 12 containing a delegation basis for safeguards on the processing of criminal-law personal data.

Naar aanleiding van het advies van de Afdeling is in artikel 12 een derde lid opgenomen, waarin een delegatiegrondslag voor het treffen van waarborgen ten aanzien van de verwerking van persoonsgegevens van strafrechtelijke aard is opgenomen.
d: rules protecting rights when processing criminal-law personal data
p: The Tax Administration decides on the compensation and on exclusion grounds, giving the receiving body discretion over which refusals qualify and whether a second refusal reason applies.
The Tax Administration may process criminal-law personal data for the scheme, with guidance and a delegated rule to protect privacy.

parties: Asks why the scheme took so long, why 2012-2013 are excluded, and about the risk of unequal treatment between groups.
These members stress that a wrongful rejection of debt restructuring is serious.
Deze leden benadrukken dat een onterechte afwijzing van schuldsanering ernstig is.
Notes the government ignored the Council of State's advice not to take irreversible steps before definitive legislation, and questions cost, implementation and legal equality.
The Council of State's advice not to take irreversible steps before definitive legislation and not to rush, because success of the policy matters more, has been disregarded by the government.

Het advies van de Raad van State om geen onomkeerbare stappen te zetten voorafgaand aan definitieve wetgeving en geen haast te maken, omdat het slagen van het tegemoetkomingsbeleid belangrijker is, is door de regering in de wind geslagen.
Welcomes government accountability for the wrongful rejections and asks for breakdowns of rejection grounds and consultation with affected citizens.
Welcomes the compensation but questions unequal treatment between citizens who repaid debts themselves and those who received only a flat 500 euro.
Asks whether a hardship clause was considered for 2012-2013 and whether the flat amount and debt-cancellation scope create legal inequality.
Was it considered to include a hardship clause in the law for this?
Is overwogen om hiervoor een hardheidsclausule in de wet op te nemen?
Supports rectifying the injustice but asks whether the flat amount is adequate, which tailored options were considered, and why citizens were not consulted beforehand.
The ChristenUnie members underline the Council of State's remark that the compensation policy was drawn up without consulting affected citizens beforehand or during its development.

De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie onderstrepen de opmerking van de Raad van State dat het «tegemoetkomingsbeleid is opgesteld zonder dat vooraf en tijdens de uitwerking ervan met betrokken burgers is gesproken».

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advises that the bill on compensating citizens wrongly refused a voluntary debt settlement (MSNP) by the Belastingdienst be reconsidered: clarify the compensation as voluntary, consult the affected group, drop the pseudo-MSNP and the bill from the Belastingdienst package. The government reply accepts the voluntary character and consultation point in part, replaces the waiting allowance with a flat EUR 500 payment, adds a statutory safeguard for personal data, removes the pre-enactment debt write-off, and removes the bill from the Belastingplan package, but keeps the pseudo-MSNP and the write-off of debts after enactment.
concerns: The Afdeling asks that the legal basis and voluntary character of the compensation be clarified, since the explanatory memorandum suggests damages without accepting liability; the government confirms the voluntary character and adjusts the allowance to a flat payment.

The Afdeling questions whether a generous financial compensation is the right instrument and whether the pseudo-MSNP is overcompensation; the government keeps the pseudo-MSNP and the debt write-off as necessary for a debt-free start.

The Afdeling objects to the scope of debt write-off, which exceeds the damage caused by the wrongful refusal, and to unequal treatment; the government drops pre-enactment write-off but keeps write-off of all open debts at enactment.
The Afdeling asks for statutory or delegated safeguards for processing personal and criminal data; the government adds a delegation basis for mandatory safeguards by AMvB.
The Afdeling doubts the feasibility and cost of implementation by 1 January 2025 and asks for justification of staffing; the government gives a revised cost estimate and keeps the timetable.

The Afdeling advises that a bill without budgetary link does not belong in the Belastingplan package and that a goedkeurend beleidsbesluit anticipating legislation should not be taken; the government removes the bill from the package and drops the anticipatory write-off.

The Afdeling advises consulting the affected citizens before finalising the scheme; the government says it has contacted various groups, but not the affected citizens directly as a formal consultation.

36684.s: The bill approves for the European part of the Netherlands the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention (No. 190), adopted in Geneva on 21 June 2019. The explanatory memorandum argues that existing Dutch equal-treatment, working-conditions and criminal law already largely meet the convention's obligations.
q: The convention aligns with Dutch legislation and practice on eliminating violence and harassment in the workplace.
Het verdrag sluit aan bij de Nederlandse wet- en regelgeving en praktijk die ziet op het uitbannen van geweld en intimidatie op de werkvloer.

parties: Asks whether the government will make explicit statutory obligations (ban on violence and harassment, risk assessment, complaint procedures, independent investigations) and extend the Arbowet and Arbeidsinspectie powers.
These members ask whether the government is willing to take a step further to eradicate violence and harassment in the workplace.
Zij vragen of de regering bereid is een stap bij te zetten om geweld en intimidatie op de werkvloer uit te bannen.
Asks whether the convention could lead to more regulation for Dutch organisations and how the government monitors that risk.
However, these members ask whether the convention could lead to an increase in rules for organisations in the Netherlands.
Wel vragen deze leden of het verdrag kan leiden tot een toename aan regels voor organisaties in Nederland.
Asks the government to justify its claim that existing law complies with the convention and to state the added value of the bill.
Finally, these members ask the government to state what exactly the added value of this bill is compared with existing policy.
Tenslotte vragen deze leden de regering om aan te geven wat precies de toegevoegde waarde is van dit wetsvoorstel ten opzichte van het staande beleid.
Asks whether the government plans new legislation to tackle boundary-crossing behaviour, given its view that no legal changes are needed.
Does the government nevertheless intend to initiate new legislation to tackle boundary-crossing behaviour vigorously?
Is de regering wel voornemens nieuwe wetgeving te initiëren om grensoverschrijdend gedrag krachtig aan te pakken?
Asks for confirmation that no additional obligations follow for government or employers, and reflection on indirect implementation via psychosocial workload and RI&E.
These members ask whether they understand correctly that no additional obligations, direct or indirect, follow from this convention for the Dutch government, employers or employees.

De leden van de CDA-fractie vragen of zij goed begrijpen dat er voor de Nederlandse overheid, voor Nederlandse werkgevers en werknemers geen aanvullende verplichtingen rechtstreeks of indirect uit dit verdrag volgen.

Finds implementation within current law insufficient and asks for a separate law, broader definitions of workers and workplace, stronger Arbeidsinspectie powers and extended criminalisation of sexual intimidation.
These members foresee insufficient implementation of the convention within current legislation and request the government to draft a separate law bundling the convention's obligations.

Deze leden voorzien onvoldoende implementatie van het verdrag binnen de huidige wetgeving en verzoeken de regering om een aparte wet op te stellen waarin de verplichtingen van het verdrag in gebundeld kunnen worden.
Asks what added value ratification has when no legislative change is needed, and how far government can be responsible for workplace safety versus employers.
Is it correct that no additional measures are currently required?
Klopt het dat er nu geen aanvullende maatregelen zijn vereist?

v.summary: The Raad van State advised that Article 5 of the ILO Convention on violence and harassment in the world of work might be a provision binding everyone under Articles 93 and 94 of the Constitution, and asked the government to specify this. The government's reply withdrew that view, holding that the treaty provisions are addressed to states and are instructional norms not capable of direct application, and revised the explanatory memorandum accordingly.
concerns: The Afdeling questioned whether Article 5 of the Convention is directly binding on everyone (self-executing) and asked for specification of which parts are binding; the government reconsidered and concluded none of the treaty provisions are self-executing.
The Afdeling asked that the explanatory memorandum clarify whether similar wording in Article 4(1) is also binding; the government addressed this by revising the general part of the memorandum.

36756.s: The bill implements the revised EU fiscal framework directive into Dutch law by amending the Wet houdbare overheidsfinanciën, replacing the MTO and debt-reduction references with the Council's recommended net expenditure path. It formally designates the Raad van State advisory division and the CPB as independent fiscal institutions with defined tasks and limits the Minister of Economic Affairs' instruction power over the CPB for those tasks.
36756.j: The memorandum justifies the bill as necessary to implement the directive's requirements on independent fiscal institutions and the ministerial independence of the CPB, rather than to expand executive powers.
q: This bill therefore contains in proposed Article 2b, third paragraph, of the Wet Hof a limitation of the instruction power of the Minister of Economic Affairs with respect to the CPB
Dit wetsvoorstel bevat daarom in het voorgestelde artikel 2b, derde lid, van de Wet Hof een beperking van de aanwijzingsbevoegdheid van de Minister van Economische Zaken ten opzichte van het CPB
p: The Minister of Economic Affairs may no longer instruct the CPB on how it performs its tasks under the directive, strengthening the independence of a fiscal oversight body from ministerial control.

parties: Asks how strict enforcement by the European Commission and the independence of budget institutions are guaranteed, and whether the excessive deficit procedure could be postponed by a new cabinet.
For these members, firm enforcement was a precondition for changing the European budget rules, the Stability and Growth Pact (SGP).
Voor de leden was een stevige handhaving randvoorwaardelijk bij de aanpassing van de Europese begrotingsregels, het Stabiliteits- en Groeipact (SGP).

Questions the robustness of the EU rules given the absence of fines, asks whether the Raad van State has the required expertise as national supervisor, and raises the cost of external evaluation for independent budget bodies.
Does the government share the view that rules without effective enforcement do not work?
Deelt de regering de mening dat regels zonder effectieve handhaving niet werken?

Supports the reform but asks why the ministerial responsibility limitation for the CPB covers only Wet HOF tasks, whether a mandatory correction plan should be retained, and whether additional resources for independent bodies will be guaranteed.
These members ask the government to explain why the bill does not again provide a correction mechanism obliging the government to draw up a recovery plan if the net expenditure path is exceeded.

De leden van de D66-fractie vragen de regering om nader toe te lichten waarom in het voorliggende wetsvoorstel niet opnieuw wordt voorzien in een correctiemechanisme, waarbij de regering wordt verplicht om een herstelplan op te stellen in geval van overschrijding van het netto-uitgavenpad.
Asks about the state of implementation in other EU member states and whether the 31 December deadline will be met EU-wide.
Will the 31 December deadline be met EU-wide?
Wordt de deadline van 31 december EU-breed gehaald?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised that the draft bill implementing the revised EU fiscal framework directive (Implementatiewet herziene Europese begrotingsregels) raises no substantive remarks and may be submitted to the Tweede Kamer. The government's reply (nader rapport) only notes that some redactional improvements were made to the explanatory memorandum.

36765.s: The bill implements the EU Critical Entities Resilience Directive (CER) in Dutch law as the Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, designating critical entities, requiring risk assessments, resilience measures and incident reporting, and giving ministers and supervisory bodies enforcement powers including administrative fines. It delegates many implementing details to AMvB and ministerial regulations and designates the relevant ministers as competent authorities.
36765.j: The memorandum justifies delegations by the need to implement the EU directive's technical and methodological details and to keep a uniform enforcement regime aligned with existing NIS1 practice.
q: Rules may be laid down by or under a general administrative order (AMvB) to implement the implementing acts, delegated acts and guidelines adopted under the CER Directive.

Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen regels worden gesteld ter uitvoering van de op grond van de CER-richtlijn vastgestelde uitvoeringshandelingen, gedelegeerde handelingen en richtsnoeren.
d: rules implementing EU implementing and delegated acts under CER
designation of critical entities by ministerial regulation or decision
designation of additional sectors, subsectors and entity categories
rules on cooperation and support to critical entities
further rules on conducting risk assessments
resilience measures and requirements per sector or entity
exempting entities covered by equivalent EU sector-specific rules
incident significance criteria and reporting modalities
exemption of entities from core obligations
p: Ministers may exempt entities from core obligations by regulation or decision in consultation with another minister, with no parliamentary approval.
Confidential information may be shared and the Wet open overheid is disapplied to it, limiting public access to information.
Authorities may impose administrative fines up to EUR 10 million or 2% of global turnover, with discretion on amount.

parties: Asks why risk assessments are assigned to sector ministers rather than the coordinating Minister of Justice and Security, and whether a standard methodology and integrated risk assessment will be used.

These members ask the government to justify why this task is assigned to sector ministers and not to the coordinating Minister of Justice and Security, who may have more knowledge on security and resilience.

Deze leden vragen de regering om te onderbouwen waarom deze taak is belegd bij vakministers en niet bij de coördinerende Minister van Justitie en Veiligheid, die mogelijk over meer kennis beschikt wat betreft veiligheid en weerbaarheid.
Asks how coherence across sectors is ensured, how overlapping supervision by multiple authorities is coordinated, and why supervision was not concentrated in a single supervisor.

Following on from this, the VVD members ask why it was not chosen to place supervision with a single supervisor with sector-specific knowledge instead of the chosen route of different supervisors per sector.

De leden van de VVD-fractie vragen in het verlengde hiervan waarom er niet voor is gekozen om het toezicht bij één toezichthouder te beleggen met sectorspecifieke kennis in plaats van de gekozen route van verschillende toezichthouders per sector.

Doubts that supervision by the Minister of the Interior over ministries designated as critical entities is sufficiently independent and asks for additional safeguards; also questions the limitation of Woo disclosure.
These members are not convinced that supervision by the Minister of the Interior and Kingdom Relations is sufficiently independent.
Deze leden zijn er niet van overtuigd dat het toezicht door de Minister van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties voldoende onafhankelijk is.
Asks whether data exchange can be limited to what is necessary, and whether the AP advice on a statutory delegation basis for personal data processing should be followed.
Can the government explain how unnecessary data exchange can be prevented as much as possible?
Kan de regering wel toelichten hoe onnodige gegevensuitwisseling zo veel mogelijk kan worden voorkomen?
Generally positive about the bill but worried about growing regulatory burden for small and medium-sized businesses and asks how many firms will be affected.
These members are however concerned about the increasing regulatory burden for smaller businesses.
Deze leden maken zich echter wel zorgen over de toenemende regeldruk voor kleinere bedrijven.
Asks how overview of the national risk assessment is kept when conducted sectorally, how the Aanpak vitaal is revised, and how overlap with the Cbw and administrative burden are avoided.
These members ask how an overview is kept of the national risk assessment when it is carried out sectorally.
Deze leden vragen op welke manier overzicht gehouden wordt over de nationale risicobeoordeling als deze sectoraal wordt uitgevoerd.
Asks why the Rechtspraak is not among the excluded public bodies in article 5 and what the reasons for the late implementation were.
These members ask the government to explain the reason for this choice.
Deze leden vragen de regering om toe te lichten met welke reden hiervoor gekozen is.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised on the draft Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten (CER directive implementation), raising points on the scope exemption for government bodies, the coordinating role of the Minister of Justice and Security, overlap with existing supervisory authorities, independence of supervision in the government sector, exemption from the Wet open overheid, and notification duties for financial and digital sector entities. The government reply accepts most points and amends the bill accordingly, including clarifying the scope exclusions, adding a cross-sector cooperation task, and adjusting notification and designation provisions.
concerns: The scope exemption for government bodies in security, defence and law enforcement should be specified in the statute itself rather than left to vague wording like 'in ieder geval'.
The coordinating role of the Minister of Justice and Security and the need for consent versus consultation on sectoral ministers' decisions should be clarified and justified.
Overlap in supervisory powers with independent administrative bodies such as ANVS should be mapped and cooperation arrangements published.
Independence of supervision over the government sector requires safeguards, with organisational measures to be examined.
The exemption of confidential information from the Wet open overheid should be motivated as necessary given existing statutory exceptions.
The bill should specify to whom confidential information may be provided and require notification to entities in the banking, financial market and digital infrastructure sectors of their obligations.
The power to designate additional sub-sectors beyond the exhaustive CER directive annex should be explained in the explanatory memorandum and the article commentary.

36783.s: The bill clarifies when a person works in the service of an employer by defining two core elements (work under employer direction and work not on one's own account and risk), with detailed indicators to be set by general administrative order. It also introduces a legal presumption of an employment contract for work paid at an hourly rate of up to €36, excluding natural persons not acting in a business capacity, and requires a report to parliament within five years.
36783.j: The memorandum justifies the delegation to a general administrative order by arguing that indicators must remain adaptable to labour-market developments and need not be fixed in formal statute.
q: By general administrative order, further rules are laid down on when there is direction by the employer.
Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur worden nadere regels gesteld over wanneer sprake is van sturing door de werkgever
d: rules on when employer direction or work at own risk exists
indexation of the hourly rate threshold to the minimum wage
amount applicable at first application after entry into force
p: Creates a legal presumption of employment for workers paid up to a threshold rate, shifting the burden toward employers and protecting workers' legal position.
Defines the employment criteria in statute while leaving detailed indicators to a general administrative order.

parties: Asks whether the criteria in the AMvB will be sent to parliament, whether prior review (voorhang) is considered, and how enforcement and the ex-post review of the presumption will work.
The GroenLinks-PvdA members ask the government to send the AMvB in which the criteria are worked out to the House.
De leden van de GroenLinks-PvdA-fractie vragen de regering de AMvB waarin de criteria zijn uitgewerkt aan de Kamer te doen toekomen.

Questions whether the codified framework will actually be effective and whether it simplifies assessment of work relationships, given the Raad van State's doubts and the weak practical effect of the presumption for vulnerable workers facing court procedures.
These members therefore ask the government to further substantiate the effectiveness of the assessment framework.
Deze leden vragen de regering daarom om de effectiviteit van het toetsingskader nader te onderbouwen.

Doubts the effectiveness of the bill, asks for justification of the lack of a robust baseline, criticises basing the clarification on platform-worker case law, and points to Raad van State and ATR advice favouring broader revision.

The D66 members ask the government to justify why it chooses to base the clarification of the employment relationship on specific case law developed for a very limited part of the labour market, namely platform workers.

De leden van de D66-fractie verzoeken de regering te motiveren waarom zij ervoor kiest de «verduidelijking» van de arbeidsrelatie te baseren op specifieke jurisprudentie die is ontwikkeld voor een zeer beperkt deel van de arbeidsmarkt, met name platformwerkers.
Asks whether a stricter distinction between self-employed and employees may lead to more contract forms through foreign constructions.
The BBB members ask whether the stricter distinction between self-employed and employees could instead lead to more contract forms through foreign constructions, according to the government.
De leden van BBB-fractie vragen of het strengere onderscheid tussen zelfstandigen en werknemers juist kan leiden tot meer contractvormen via buitenlandse constructies volgens de regering.

Supports the presumption but questions the codification of case law, the role of the judge in civil law, the hard-coded fixed order of criteria, and whether less far-reaching instruments than a major statutory change were considered.
These members ask whether the government can further reflect on the role of the judge in civil law and the desirability of codifying case law.
Deze leden vragen of de regering nader kan reflecteren op de rol van de rechter in het civiel recht en de wenselijkheid om jurisprudentie te codificeren.

Asks the government to split the bill and pass the presumption first, to submit the AMvB to the Staten-Generaal, and to reconsider the narrow reading of free substitution and the extrapolation of case law to diverse self-employed.
They have therefore already repeatedly advised the government to split this bill and let the presumption pass the Staten-Generaal first.
Zij hebben de regering daarom reeds verschillende keren aangeraden dit wetsvoorstel te splitsen en het rechtsvermoeden met voorrang door de Staten-Generaal te laten gaan.
Has no additional questions for now and awaits the report and further treatment.
For now these members have no additional questions.
Voor nu hebben deze leden geen aanvullende vragen.
Asks when the government would consider a new normative framework or new case law/legislation, and why the 36 euro threshold was chosen rather than a higher or lower one.
These members are curious in which scenario the government would consider drawing up a new normative framework.
Deze leden zijn benieuwd in welk scenario er wel gekeken wordt naar het opstellen van een nieuw normenkader?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advises that the bill on working 'in dienst van' (employment relationship criterion and a rebuttable presumption of employment at an hourly rate of €33 or less) only modestly addresses the underlying problems of bogus self-employment, and raises concerns about pension premium frictions, the effectiveness of the test framework, and possible divergent classifications. The government's nader rapport largely disagrees on the broader framing, agrees to clarify pension premium risks and the test framework in the explanatory memorandum, and states it has revised the bill (e.g. external entrepreneurship as a standalone indicator).
concerns: The bill contributes only modestly to solving the identified problems, mainly codifying existing law, and the broader structural problem is not addressed; the government responds that the bill is part of an integrated three-line approach.

The proposed test framework may not make qualification in practice simpler or more effective given the casuistic nature of the assessment; the government argues effectiveness depends on the wider integrated approach and communication.

The rebuttable presumption may lead to divergent qualifications, since implementing bodies keep their own investigative duty; the government disagrees that the risk is increased but does not add clarifying provisions.

Pension premium arrears from retroactive reclassification as employment contract pose risks for pension funds; the government explains the 'no premium, still entitlement' principle and possible exceptions, and the explanatory memorandum is adapted accordingly.

The Afdeling notes that the bill does not solve the broader vulnerability of workers, including genuine self-employed and flex workers, and warns of waterbed effects toward other flexible arrangements such as secondment.

The Afdeling advises discussing the question of more autonomy in work in the explanatory memorandum; the government acknowledges this and points to flexible arrangements available within employment contracts.

36792.s: The bill amends the Wet tegemoetkomingen loondomein so that a new employer can claim the remaining duration of a wage-cost advantage (loonkostenvoordeel) for disabled workers, by linking the doelgroepverklaring to the employer rather than only the worker. It adds transitional rules and specifies that UWV issues the new-employer declaration only after checking prior declarations, beschut werk status and AOW age.
36792.j: The memorandum justifies the change by pointing to two court rulings (CRvB, 22 March 2023) and the need for a structural, robust way for a new employer to continue the wage-cost advantage, with privacy considerations for the worker.
q: This bill therefore first provides that a doelgroepverklaring is not only granted to a specific worker but is also linked to the employer.
Dit wetsvoorstel regelt daarom allereerst dat een doelgroepverklaring niet alleen wordt verleend aan een specifieke werknemer, maar ook wordt gekoppeld aan de werkgever.
d: Artikel I, B.3 (art. 2.6 lid 3 nieuw) and C.2 (art. 2.7 lid 3 nieuw)
UWV issuing new-employer doelgroepverklaring under conditions in the Act

parties: Asks the government about the reasons for not applying the law retroactively, how transitional arrangements will be communicated, whether UWV has received an implementation order, and when the Wtl evaluation takes place.
These members ask for further explanation of why it was not chosen to give this law retroactive effect.
Deze leden vragen om nadere toelichting waarom er niet is gekozen om deze wet met terugwerkende kracht te laten gelden.

Worries that the administrative burden falls one-sidedly on employees with limited administrative or digital skills, and asks whether employers should be obliged to assist and inform workers and what concrete support will be offered.
Does the government agree with the D66 group that it is undesirable to place this administrative burden solely on the employee?
Is de regering het met de D66-fractie eens dat het onwenselijk is om deze administratieve last eenzijdig bij de werknemer te leggen?

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division supports extending the wage-cost subsidy to workers who take a new job, but raises a privacy and administrative-burden concern: after a business transfer the worker must request a new doelgroepverklaring or authorise the employer, and the new employer depends on the worker's cooperation despite being legally obliged to pay wages. The government's reply defends the two-step system on privacy and UWV verification grounds and clarifies the explanatory memorandum, without changing the bill substantively.
concerns: The Afdeling questions whether the extra administrative step for workers after a business transfer is necessary, given that only the payroll number changes; the government maintains the two-step procedure for privacy and verification reasons but clarifies the memorandum.

The Afdeling notes the new employer depends on the worker's cooperation to keep the subsidy while legally bearing the full wage obligation, a point the government answers by saying the employer can expect most workers to authorise it, without changing the design.

The Afdeling observes that privacy concerns seem smaller where only the employer's payroll number changes; the government agrees this holds for pure changes of legal form but explains privacy applies in other transfers.

36819.s: The bill adds rules implementing the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism regulation to the Environmental Management Act, making breaches of named CBAM provisions prohibited and enforceable by the emissions authority NEa through periodic penalties and administrative fines. It also lets ministers set further rules by ministerial regulation, assigns sale and repurchase of CBAM certificates to the Minister of Finance, and creates a legal basis for sharing confidential information with third parties.
36819.j: The memorandum justifies the ministerial regulation powers by the need to respond quickly to later EU delegated and implementing acts while keeping the delegation to binding parts only.
q: That way, swift action can be taken if the interest of smooth implementation of the regulation requires it.
Op die manier kan voortvarend worden gereageerd indien het belang van een soepele uitvoering van de verordening dat vereist.
d: designating further regulatory provisions whose breach is prohibited
rules implementing binding parts of the CBAM regulation and EU acts
further rules for sale and repurchase of CBAM certificates
p: Allows the minister, by ministerial regulation, to add new provisions whose breach becomes a punishable offence, with the memorandum saying this basis will be used as little as possible and later replaced by statute.
Allows the emissions authority to share confidential information with other persons where confidentiality is assured.
Gives the emissions authority power to impose administrative fines and periodic penalties for breaches, with fixed minimum fine amounts that the authority cannot reduce.

parties: Questions the outsourcing of CBAM licensing to a commercial party despite Council of State criticism and asks why alternatives were not chosen.

These members therefore ask the government to explain how the House was involved in the decision to outsource, which alternative options were considered to prevent outsourcing and mandating to an external commercial party, and why none of these options was chosen.

Deze leden vragen de regering daarom om toe te lichten hoe de Kamer betrokken is bij de keuze tot uitbesteding, welke alternatieve opties zijn overwogen om uitbesteding en mandatering van een externe commerciële partij te voorkomen en waarom niet voor één van deze opties is gekozen.
Supports effective climate policy but stresses competitiveness; asks how enforcement, legal protection of companies and periodic evaluation with reporting to parliament will be ensured.
The VVD members attach importance to a watertight and feasible enforcement regime.</br>
De leden van de VVD-fractie hechten aan een sluitend en uitvoerbaar handhavingsregime.

Doubts the delegation power to ministerial regulations for prohibitions, citing legal uncertainty, and asks how the period of uncertainty will be mitigated and how the PwC arrangement was decided with the House.
The members of the D66 group have some question marks about the delegation power.
De leden van de D66-fractie hebben enkele vraagtekens bij de delegatiebevoegdheid.
Supports CBAM but asks about effects on exporters, marginal versus average cost issues and downstream products outside the scheme.
The ChristenUnie members are in favour of the CBAM system, but have a number of questions about the consequences of this border levy.</br>
De leden van de ChristenUnie-fractie zijn voorstander van het CBAM-systeem, maar hebben een aantal vragen over de gevolgen van deze grensheffing.

Asks about effective supervision and international cooperation, the Council of State's criticism of mandating to a commercial party, and objects to amending the regulation via ministerial regulation without a formal legislative route.
The Council of State is critical of this and these members share that view.
De Raad van State is hier kritisch op en deze leden delen dat.

v.summary: The Raad van State advisory division advised against submitting the bill on the CBAM carbon border adjustment as drafted, unless amended, raising concerns about outsourcing NEa tasks to a commercial firm (PwC) under mandate, data confidentiality, GDPR roles, and broad ministerial-regulation delegation for future CBAM changes. The government's reply largely accepts the points: it will withdraw the mandate to the project director, add a statutory confidentiality-sharing provision, clarify PwC as processor, and commits to limiting the delegation, though it keeps the ministerial-regulation power.
concerns: The Afdeling advises replacing the ministerial-regulation delegation for future CBAM amendments with statutory regulation and delegating to an AMvB; the government keeps the ministerial regulation power but commits to limiting its use and reconsidering it later.

Outsourcing NEa tasks via mandate to a commercial firm with an advisory and tax arm raises constitutional and conflict-of-interest concerns; the government withdraws the mandate to the project director, leaving PwC only in a preparatory role.
Ministerial regulations can change prohibited conduct without parliamentary involvement, harming legal certainty; government adds nuance but keeps the approach.
Confidential information sharing with an external party needs a statutory basis and confidentiality safeguards; government adds an explicit statutory provision.
Explanatory memorandum lacks explanation of why tasks were outsourced and of GDPR controller/processor roles; government supplements the explanation.
The financial section was missing from the request; it has been completed.

36820-III.s: The bill amends the 2025 budget statements for the Ministry of General Affairs, the Cabinet of the King, and the Commission for Oversight of Intelligence and Security Services, through a September supplementary budget. It sets the amounts in thousands of euros and makes the amendments retroactive to 16 September 2025.

36846.s: The bill inserts new articles into the Bankwet 1998 requiring banks, investment funds, pension funds and insurers to report loan-level data on mortgages for homes and commercial property to De Nederlandsche Bank, replacing the existing request power. It also restricts DNB's onward sharing of that data, limits internal sharing, and adds a penalty power for enforcing the reporting rules.
36846.j: The memorandum justifies the reporting duty as necessary for DNB's financial stability and statistical tasks, with data minimisation, a ban on re-identification and onward disclosure, and a 12-year retention limit as safeguards.
q: The data will in no case be used by DNB to take decisions concerning these persons or in a way that affects or could affect their social position.

De gegevens worden door DNB in geen geval gebruikt om besluiten te nemen ten aanzien van deze betrokkenen of op een wijze die de maatschappelijke positie van deze betrokkenen raakt of zou kunnen raken.
d: reporting content, periodicity, deadlines and size threshold for loan-level mortgage data
electronic submission format and login method
method of pseudonymising residential mortgage data
