p: Creates a mandatory loan-level reporting duty on financial firms covering identifiable borrowers, expanding DNB's information access beyond the former request power, with data minimisation and pseudonymisation as safeguards.
Allows internal sharing of the data across DNB units under conditions of non-structural, anonymised use and only where the data could have been obtained directly from supervised firms.
Gives DNB power to impose a penalty order to enforce the new reporting rules.

parties: Supports the bill but insists that financial stability monitoring must not come at the expense of citizens' privacy.
These members find safeguarding financial stability extremely important, but find it just as important that this does not come at the expense of people's privacy.
Deze leden vinden het borgen van de financiële stabiliteit uiterst belangrijk, maar vinden het net zo belangrijk dat dit niet ten koste gaat van de privacy van mensen.
Asks about proportionality, data minimisation, need-to-know versus nice-to-know data, and legal certainty for reporting parties and borrowers.

These members endorse the importance of a stable financial system and adequate risk monitoring, but also attach great importance to proportionality, data minimisation, reducing regulatory burden and legal certainty for reporting parties.

Deze leden onderschrijven het belang van een stabiel financieel stelsel en adequate monitoring van risico’s, maar hechten tevens groot belang aan proportionaliteit, dataminimalisatie, regeldrukbeperking en rechtszekerheid voor rapportageplichtige partijen.
Supports the reporting duty but questions DNB's past capacity without specified data, the 12-year retention rule instead of deletion, and the lack of a sunset clause.
These members ask why deletion of data is not chosen, so that one can be certain it can never be misused later.
Deze leden vragen de regering waarom niet wordt gekozen voor verwijderen van gegevens, zodat je zeker weet dat er nooit alsnog op een onbehoorlijke manier mee omgegaan kan worden.
Welcomes monitoring of mortgage risks in principle but argues monitoring alone does not reduce risks and asks about measures for debt sustainability.
although monitoring data can give a better picture of risks in the mortgage market, monitoring alone cannot ensure those risks decline.
hoewel het monitoren van gegevens een beter beeld kan geven van risico’s op de hypotheekmarkt, alleen monitoren er niet voor kan zorgen dat deze risico’s afnemen.

Criticises the broad collection of personal data, the risk of identifiability, the vague delegation to a general administrative order, and the weak retention rules; echoes the Raad van State's critique.
Does this not precisely lead to a much greater chance of personal data being traceable?
Leidt dit niet juist tot veel grotere kans op herleidbaarheid van persoonsgegevens?

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised clarifying the necessity of the DNB mortgage reporting bill, justifying the level of detail (postcode, birth year, income) given the data-minimisation and re-identification risks, and making the internal data-sharing safeguard unambiguous in the bill text. The minister's reply states the explanatory memorandum was supplemented on necessity and detail levels, the internal-sharing safeguard was added to article 9e, and several articles were restructured.
concerns: The Afdeling asked for a fuller explanation of why the bill is necessary for DNB's statistical and financial stability tasks, which the minister addressed by expanding the explanatory memorandum.

The Afdeling questioned whether sensitive fine-grained data (birth year, four postcode digits, income) are necessary, and asked why further aggregation is not possible; the minister justified the detail level and adopted aggregation safeguards by rule of general administrative order.
The Afdeling found the bill ambiguous on whether internal data sharing within DNB could be systematic, and advised unambiguous wording; the minister added a safeguard to article 9e.
The minister restructured the reporting obligation over several articles and added an exemption provision for readability and lighter burden.

36850-X.s: This second supplementary budget amends the 2025 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Defence, raising commitments and expenditure by about EUR 298.5 million and EUR 689.8 million respectively. The bill sets the amounts in thousands of euros and takes effect retroactively from 1 December 2025.
q: We ... with joint consultation of the States General, have approved ... The departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Defence (X) for 2025 is amended
Wij Willem-Alexander ... hebben goedgevonden en verstaan ... De departementale begrotingsstaat van het Ministerie van Defensie (X) voor het jaar 2025 wordt gewijzigd

36855.s: The bill inserts a sentence into article 108a of the Aliens Act 2000 providing that participating in the offence of illegal residence, other than as a principal perpetrator, is not punishable, so that humanitarian helpers avoid complicity liability. The explanatory memorandum responds to an advisory opinion of the Council of State warning that aiding illegal residents could be punishable as co-perpetration or complicity.
36855.j: The memorandum justifies the exemption by arguing that helpers acting from humanitarian or professional duties should not be criminalised, and that the Council of State advised that complicity liability is a realistic risk.
q: The cabinet considers that providing assistance should not be punishable.
Het kabinet vindt dat hulpverlening niet strafbaar moet zijn.

parties: Questions the balancing of interests and the sound preparation of the bill and asks for an ex ante implementation test; worries people may be prosecuted without fault.
No sound balancing of interests has taken place regarding the desirability of the proposal.</reasoning_effort>
Er heeft geen deugdelijke belangenafweging plaatsgevonden over de wenselijkheid van het voorstel.
Supports criminalising illegality as a deterrent but objects that facilitating illegal residence is left unpunished.
The government now chooses to leave facilitating illegal residence unpunished.</reasoning_effort>
De regering kiest er nu voor om het faciliteren van illegaal verblijf straffeloos te laten.
Doubts effectiveness and legal feasibility, criticises disregard of implementing bodies' and experts' advice, and questions the impact on aid and fundamental rights.
This raises the question to what extent the government is truly open to expert advice that does not fit its agenda.</reasoning_effort>
Dat roept de vraag op in hoeverre de regering echt openstaat voor adviezen van deskundigen die niet in haar straatje passen.
Criticises adoption of the underlying amendment without debate and asks about the difference with the Raad van State's proposed exemption and the inconsistency between the three criminal provisions.
Has no questions on the novelle.
The BBB fractie has taken note of the novelle and has no questions about it.</reasoning_effort>
De leden van de BBB-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van de novelle en hebben hier geen vragen over.
Objects to retaining criminalisation despite broad criticism of effectiveness, proportionality and feasibility, and questions the cabinet's demissionary mandate.
Accepts criminalisation as a last resort while insisting humanitarian help is exempt; asks about necessity defences, overlap with trafficking and EU directive.
They consider it of great importance that it is crystal clear that help out of humanity is under no circumstances punishable.</reasoning_effort>
Zij vinden het van groot belang dat glashelder is dat hulp uit medemenselijkheid onder geen beding strafbaar wordt.
Objects to the haste that undermines careful preparation and asks why the Raad van State's warnings are ignored; raises proportionality and protection concerns.
The haste with which the already adopted article 108a Vw is being repaired with this novelle undermines the required care.</reasoning_effort>
De spoed waarmee het reeds aangenomen artikel 108a Vw met deze novelle wordt «gerepareerd», doet afbreuk aan de vereiste zorgvuldigheid.
Objects to the flawed legislative process and the unusual construction leaving prosecution possible, leaving legal certainty to courts; questions proportionality.
Does the government not shift responsibility for legal certainty and legal protection to the courts in this way?</reasoning_effort>
Schuift de regering de verantwoordelijkheid voor rechtszekerheid en rechtsbescherming op deze manier niet naar de rechtspraak?
Raises fundamental rights, child welfare, access to care and EU Return Directive concerns and asks how the government will safeguard them.

v.summary: The Raad van State's Afdeling advisering advises that the criminalisation of illegal stay in the Asylum Emergency Measures Act, introduced by amendment, be scrutinised further, and that the novelle excluding all forms of participation (other than as perpetrator) be explained in relation to criminal law systematics and to existing offences of illegal stay. The government's reply defends the spoedige behandeling and the exclusion of helpers, and adds clarifications to the explanatory memorandum without changing the core of the bill.
concerns: The Afdeling notes that the exclusion of all forms of participation departs from criminal law systematics and that the novelle does not cover existing offences of illegal stay with entry bans, so the bill and memorandum should be adjusted; the government added explanation but kept the exclusion.

The Afdeling questions whether the criminalisation of illegal stay is necessary and effective given existing offences and the consultation concerns, and advises it be dealt with in a separate bill; the government declined to remove it from the Asylum Emergency Measures Act.

The Afdeling finds the preparation of the criminalisation of illegal stay not careful and an integrated weighing of interests not carried out; the government responds that the Tweede Kamer determines its own procedure and that urgency outweighed this.

The Afdeling asks for clarification whether the exception is a prosecution-exclusion or a qualification-exclusion ground; the government explains it is a special exception leading to dismissal of prosecution and adds this to the memorandum.

36864.s: The bill amends the Omgevingswet, Wet milieubeheer and Wet belastingen op milieugrondslag to implement the revised Industrial Emissions Directive and the PIE regulation on reporting of industrial environmental data, adding intensive livestock installations and a Portaal Industriële Emissies. It updates definitions, publication duties and cross-references, with detailed rules to follow in an amvb.
36864.j: The memorandum justifies the amvb delegation by saying the detailed implementation of the revised directive will mainly take place at amvb level, with the explanatory notes to that decree providing further detail.
q: The adjustment of regulations in connection with the revised IED and the PIE regulation will mainly take place at the level of a general administrative measure (amvb).
De aanpassing van regelgeving in verband met de herziene Rie en de PIE-verordening zal voornamelijk plaatsvinden op het niveau van een algemene maatregel van bestuur
d: Artikel I, onderdeel D (Omgevingswet art. 5.38, tweede lid)
uniform conditions for implementing rules for intensive livestock installations
p: Artikel I, onderdeel H, punt 5 and onderdeel E (ongewoon voorval, enforcement)
Broadens the definition of unusual incidents by reference to the directive, giving the competent authority enforcement grounds without substantive change to its discretion.

parties: Asks that parliament is informed early about policy choices in the AMvB and that the tight timeline does not undermine parliamentary involvement.
These members ask whether the government can guarantee that the tight entry-into-force deadline of 1 July 2026 does not undermine the care of parliamentary involvement in this AMvB.
Deze leden vragen of de regering kan garanderen dat de strakke inwerkingtredingstermijn van 1 juli 2026 de zorgvuldigheid van de parlementaire betrokkenheid bij deze amvb niet in de weg staat.
Asks whether affected sectors were informed and whether the impact and feasibility of compliance are sufficiently assessed.
Furthermore, the VVD members ask how, given that no consultation has taken place, it has been established that the impact on these sectors is limited, as stated.
Daarnaast vragen de leden van de VVD-fractie hoe, nu er geen consultatie heeft plaatsgevonden, is vastgesteld dat de impact voor deze sectoren beperkt is, zoals wordt gesteld.
Has no further questions on the bill.
The CDA members have taken note of the bill and have no further questions.
De leden van de CDA-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en hebben geen verdere vragen.
Worries about workability and enforcement arbitrariness for livestock farmers, including the vague 'substantial deterioration' threshold for closures and sanction proportionality.
Can the government clarify the lower limit for a 'substantial deterioration', and how is it guaranteed that this measure is not used lightly for minor technical violations posing no direct danger?

Kan de regering nader duiden wat de ondergrens is voor een «aanzienlijke verslechtering», en hoe wordt gewaarborgd dat dit middel niet lichtvaardig wordt ingezet bij kleine technische overtredingen die geen direct gevaar vormen?
Fears industry dominance in drafting, demands independent health and environmental expert involvement, stronger enforcement capacity and independent monitoring.

These members are very concerned that the close involvement of industry in drafting this proposal means it is mainly economically good for industry but has too few positive effects on protecting our health and environment.

Deze leden maken zich grote zorgen dat de nauwe betrokkenheid van de industrie bij het uitwerken van dit voorstel ervoor zorgt dat het voorstel vooral economisch goed is voor de industrie, maar te weinig positieve effecten heeft op de bescherming van onze gezondheid en het milieu.

v.summary: The Raad van State advised on a bill implementing the revised Industrial Emissions Directive and the PIE Regulation, raising concerns about the clarity of the transposition (missing transposition tables), the sanctions criteria, and the transitional law for IPPC installations. The government's nader rapport reports that the explanatory memorandum, transposition tables and transitional provisions were revised in response to the advice.
concerns: The transposition table for the revised IED omitted provisions already implemented at statutory level, and no transposition table was included for the PIE Regulation; the government added a PIE table and expanded the table for the IED.

The bill did not address transitional law for IPPC installations under the revised directive, which the explanatory memorandum omitted; the government expanded the explanatory memorandum and amended the bill accordingly.

Implementation of the sanctions criteria and the choice between administrative and criminal sanctions required clearer explanation; the government added justification in the explanatory memorandum, arguing existing Dutch law already complies.
Access-to-justice provisions were to be explained more fully in line with the Aarhus Convention and the Varkens-in-Noodarrest ruling; the explanatory memorandum was expanded accordingly.

36873.s: The bill implements EU Directive 2024/825 on consumer protection for the green transition by amending Book 6 of the Dutch Civil Code, adding definitions and new rules on environmental claims, sustainability labels, durability and software updates, and information duties. It introduces prohibited practices in B2C commerce and requires traders to give specified product information, with enforcement by the ACM as a regulator operating under existing consumer law.
36873.j: The memorandum justifies the bill as necessary to transpose a maximum-harmonisation EU directive, with no delegation or new executive powers proposed.
q: The trader must inform the consumer of the existence and duration of a commercial durability guarantee (manufacturer's guarantee) where the producer offers it free of charge, for more than two years and for the whole product.

Zo moet de handelaar de consument informeren over het bestaan en de duur van een commerciële garantie van duurzaamheid (fabrieksgarantie), in het geval dat deze gratis, voor meer dan twee jaar en met betrekking tot het hele goed wordt aangeboden door de producent.

parties: Asks how the information duties will be made understandable and comparable, how the regulatory burden is estimated, and whether the ACM has the capacity to enforce the new tasks.
What additional capacity, expertise or resources does the ACM need to carry out these new tasks properly, and are they structurally secured?
Welke extra capaciteit, expertise of middelen zijn bij de ACM nodig om deze nieuwe taken goed uit te voeren, en zijn die structureel geborgd?
Asks how the rules apply to non-EU firms exporting to the EU and how enforcement works for foreign webshops, and whether the maximum harmonisation leaves room for national choices.
In addition, the VVD members ask whether companies not established in EU countries but exporting goods to the European internal market must also comply with these rules for labels.

Daarnaast vragen de leden van de VVD-fractie of bedrijven die niet in landen binnen de EU zijn gevestigd, maar die wel goederen naar landen binnen de Europese interne markt exporteren, ook aan deze regels voor keurmerken moeten voldoen.
Has taken note of the bill and the amendment note and has no further questions at this point.
The CDA members have taken note of the bill and the amendment note and have no further questions on it at this moment.
De leden van de CDA-fractie hebben kennisgenomen van het wetsvoorstel en de nota van wijziging en hebben daarover op dit moment geen verdere vragen.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised, without substantive remarks, that the bill implementing Directive (EU) 2024/825 on consumer protection against greenwashing and unfair practices be submitted to parliament. The government's reply notes that a conflict-rule provision was added regarding the related bill on distance financial services, and that some editorial and legislative-technical changes were made.

36882.s: The bill amends the Wet langdurige zorg so that, when a verzekerde cannot file an application themselves and no legal representative or written authorised agent acts, a spouse, registered partner or other partner may apply, and failing them a parent, child, sibling or grandparent/grandchild may apply for a Wlz indication, without first obtaining guardianship from a court. It also extends the family-member application route in article 8.1.2 and removes the previous special regime for persons under Wzd measures.
36882.j: The memorandum justifies the change by arguing that guardianship procedures are slow, costly and often refused, delaying access to necessary care, and that the CIZ assessment provides sufficient safeguards.
q: Enabling family members to also file a Wlz application will be an important simplification for family members compared with the current situation.
Het mogelijk maken dat familieleden voortaan ook een Wlz-aanvraag mogen doen, betekent voor familieleden een belangrijke vereenvoudiging ten opzichte van de huidige situatie
p: Family members gain the ability to file a Wlz application on behalf of an incapable insured person without court-appointed guardianship, with the CIZ examining the application and its basis.

parties: Supports the bill as guaranteeing access to the Wlz for people who cannot apply themselves.

The D66 members stress the importance of this bill, which guarantees access to the Wet langdurige zorg by allowing family members to submit an application when the insured person can no longer do so and no legal representative or authorisation has been arranged.

De leden van de D66-fractie onderstrepen het belang van dit wetsvoorstel, dat de toegankelijkheid van de Wet langdurige zorg waarborgt door familieleden de mogelijkheid te geven een aanvraag in te dienen wanneer de verzekerde dat zelf niet meer kan en er geen wettelijk vertegenwoordiger of machtiging is geregeld.
Has no further questions at this stage.
At this moment they have no further questions on this.
Op het moment hebben zij hierbij geen verdere vragen.
Asks how it is guaranteed that an application is made voluntarily and that applicants understand their rights and duties, and how the CIZ assesses doubt.
Could it be further explained how it is guaranteed that this happens of free will and that the applicant sufficiently understands the rights and duties of the application?
Zou nader toegelicht kunnen worden op welke wijze gewaarborgd wordt dat dit uit vrije wil gebeurt en de aanvrager de rechten en plichten van de aanvraag voldoende overziet?
Wants self-determination protected and asks how often the problem occurs, how CIZ handles family conflict and whether effects can be monitored early.
They ask how it is handled when several family members apply or contradict each other and how delay for the client is prevented.
Ook vragen zij hoe wordt gehandeld wanneer meerdere familieleden zich melden of elkaar tegenspreken en hoe vertraging voor de cliënt wordt voorkomen.
Has no questions for the Minister.
The members have no questions for the Minister.
De leden hebben geen vragen aan de Minister.
Supports the bill and urges swift treatment and introduction, asking for the intended effective date.
These members urge swift treatment and introduction of the law.
Deze leden dringen aan op een snelle behandeling en invoering van de wet.
Asks how voluntary care is ensured when people can no longer sign an application themselves, and how this relates to the Wzd and Wvggz routes.
They ask what this looks like in practice when people are no longer able to sign a Wlz application themselves.
Zij vragen hoe dit in praktijk eruit ziet als mensen niet meer zelf in staat zijn om een Wlz-aanvraag te ondertekenen.
Supports the amendment as removing an unnecessary barrier to Wlz care and avoiding extra administrative burden.
Therefore the members of Groep Markuszower endorse the necessity of this amendment and have no further questions or comments on it.
Daarom onderschrijven de leden van de Groep Markuszower de noodzaak van deze wetswijziging en hebben zij daarover geen nadere vragen of opmerkingen.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State raised no remarks on the draft bill amending the Wet langdurige zorg to allow family members to apply for a Wlz indication, and advised submitting it to the Tweede Kamer. The government's reply clarifies that the aim is to safeguard access to the Wlz and explains that the circle of applicants is limited to those who may act as representatives under the Wzd and the Civil Code, to keep the infringement on self-determination no greater than necessary.
concerns: The restriction of the circle of applicants to statutory representatives was adjusted to keep the infringement on the right of self-determination no greater than necessary.

36915-V.s: This first supplementary budget amends the 2026 departmental budget statement of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, adjusting commitments, expenditures and receipts across policy and non-policy articles. The bill takes effect the day after publication in the Staatsblad and applies retroactively from 1 June 2026.
36915-V.j: The memorandum justifies the budget changes by adjusting receipts to CEP forecasts and realistic timing, with no delegation of power.
q: This is an adjustment of the collection cost compensation based on the CEP forecasts for 2026.
Dit is een aanpassing van de perceptiekostenvergoeding op basis van de CEP-ramingen van 2026.

36918.s: The bill makes the temporary counter-terrorism administrative measures act permanent by removing its sunset provision, and deletes the power to refuse or withdraw permits and decisions where they could aid terrorism (article 6 and related provisions). It replaces the earlier sunset with a report to parliament due by 1 March 2032 on the act's effectiveness.
36918.j: The memorandum justifies permanence by the lasting need for administrative measures to protect national security, based on the evaluation's findings, and notes that the measures were hardly used.
q: because of the lasting need to have administrative measures available to protect national security
vanwege de blijvende noodzaak om te kunnen beschikken over bestuurlijke maatregelen ter bescherming van de nationale veiligheid
p: Removing the sunset clause and the horizon provision makes the Minister's power to impose movement and contact restrictions permanent, while the only remaining safeguard is a report due in 2032.

v.summary: The Afdeling advisering of the Raad van State advised critically on the bill to make the Tijdelijke wet bestuurlijke maatregelen terrorismebestrijding permanent, questioning necessity given a critical evaluation, changed threat picture (rechts-terrorisme), and meldplicht effectiveness. The government's nader rapport partly accepts the points by adding explanations and changes to the explanatory memorandum but maintains the bill and the necessity of the measures.
concerns: The Afdeling doubts the necessity of the measures given a critical evaluation finding the law not a necessary instrument; the government maintains the bill, arguing the measures remain of added value.
The measures may interfere with fundamental rights such as freedom of movement, privacy and association, and EU free movement, requiring thorough justification of necessity.
The changed nature of the threat, including right-wing terrorism, raises whether the powers still fit; the government added explanation in the memorie van toelichting but did not change the bill.
Effectiveness of the meldplicht as a contact moment is doubtful; the government refers to a guideline for professionals and clarifies the purpose is national security rather than deradicalisation.

36927.s: The bill implements Regulation (EU) 2024/900 on transparency and targeting of political advertising in the Netherlands by designating the Commissariaat voor de Media, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and the ACM as competent authorities with supervisory and enforcement powers, including entry into homes without the occupant's consent, binding instructions, administrative fines and binding commitments. It also exempts these authorities from several Kaderwet zbo provisions to secure their independence and adds a register and information-sharing regime involving the Napp.
36927.j: The memorandum justifies the powers by the need for fully independent and effective supervisors able to enforce the regulation's transparency and targeting requirements.
q: The Commissariaat and the AP regarding Article 20 have a number of powers that follow from Article 22(5) of this regulation.
Het Commissariaat en de AP met betrekking tot artikel 20 hebben een aantal bevoegdheden die volgen uit artikel 22, vijfde lid, van deze verordening.
p: Article 6 lets the Commissariaat and the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens enter a home without the occupant's consent, limited to what is reasonably necessary for their powers under the General Administrative Law Act.
Article 6 grants the authorities power to impose binding instructions, provisional measures, orders under administrative coercion and administrative fines for breaches of the regulation.
Article 7 lets the authorities make violators' commitments binding, extend their duration and modify or withdraw such decisions in defined cases.
Article 8 disapplies the minister's power to set policy rules, to annul decisions and to intervene in serious neglect of duties for the designated authorities, to protect their independence.

v.summary: The Council of State's Advisory Division advised on the draft Uitvoeringswet implementing the EU regulation on transparency and targeting of political advertising, raising concerns about the definition of political advertising, the choice of the Commissariaat voor de Media as supervisor, deviation from the Kaderwet zbo's, targeting, and public accountability. The government's reply (nader rapport) largely accepts the points, clarifies the definition and the implementation, and adjusts the bill in several respects, while keeping the Kaderwet deviation for the AP and ACM and the choice of supervisor.
concerns: The Division asked for clarification of the notion of political advertising and whether additional targeting measures are needed; the government clarified the definition via Commission guidelines but saw no need yet for additional national measures.

The exclusion of ministerial powers under the Kaderwet zbo's (policy rules, annulment) was insufficiently motivated; the government kept the exclusion for AP and ACM but reinstated article 23 for the Commissariaat.
The choice of the Commissariaat voor de Media as supervisor needed fuller justification relative to the ACM and the DSA; the government added reasoning and clarified resources.
Concerns about adequate technical, financial and personnel resources for supervisors were addressed by pointing to structurally allocated funds.
Public consultation and accountability on supervisors' policy rules and the theme of political advertising needed concrete elaboration; the memorandum was supplemented.
Non-application to Caribbean Netherlands needed better justification; the government explained the reasons and supplemented the explanatory memorandum.
Several technical adjustments were made, including powers of entry, binding instructions, deletion of article 7 and an amended entry-into-force provision.

36936.s: The bill amends the Environmental Management Act and the Economic Offences Act to introduce an annual obligation for operators of industrial installations to use renewable non-biological hydrogen fuels, tracked in a new HWI register run by the NEa. It sets detailed rules on quotas, verification, registration, trading, sanctions and a delegated framework to be fleshed out by AMvB and ministerial regulation.
36936.j: The memorandum justifies the delegations by the need for technical detail, flexibility to adjust the annual obligation, and the NEa's experience with the comparable transport obligation.
d: exempting categories of industrial installations from the obligation
percentage annual obligation and calculation rules
conditions and calculation rules for exempt hydrogen categories
period and conditions for registering hydrogen without proof of sustainability
rules on operation, organisation and security of the HWI register
refusal, blocking or closure of accounts for suspected fraud or misuse
postponement of the annual obligation to a later year
ex officio determination of registered quantities
p: The NEa may unilaterally determine quantities of registered fuel up to five years back, reducing the regulated party's certainty.
The NEa may suspend or refuse crediting of HWI units on suspicion of misuse or fraud, without a stated evidentiary threshold.
The NEa may refuse, block or close accounts where it suspects fraud or non-compliance, with details left to an AMvB.
Producers, importers and suppliers of hydrogen must provide data to the NEa on request, with the data set left to ministerial regulation.
The NEa may impose administrative fines up to the sixth category or 10% of turnover, and may bar a repeat offender from crediting renewable fuels for a period it sets.

v.summary: The Council of State's advisory division (10 December 2025) advises that the annual renewable hydrogen obligation for industrial installations may not be sufficient to meet the member-state target under RED Article 22bis, and raises legal-basis and formulation concerns about the ammonia-production exemptions. The government's nader rapport (23 April 2026) accepts several points (clarifying the existing-installation condition, expanding explanation in the memorandum) and explains why it keeps the 4% target and the exemptions while acknowledging remaining uncertainty.
concerns: The instrument mix may not be sufficient to reach the RED Article 22bis target in 2030 and 2035, and the explanatory memorandum should justify its suitability or set out additional steps.
The ammonia-production exemptions lack a sufficient basis in RED articles, since recitals and Commission declarations are not binding, and they create legal uncertainty.
The exemption for ammonia production from steam methane reforming is broader than the recital and Commission declaration, which concern only existing installations, and should be aligned with them.
The explanation of how the reliability of the claimed greenhouse gas reductions is guaranteed should be clarified.
